classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/15 plus mins/Introduce-to-Maintenance Cards
title: Introduce-to-Maintenance Cards
best_used_for: When high-line customers are walking at the cash-out, or your advisors are dreading the big conversation.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your manufacturer's maintenance schedule for your top models and a blank maintenance card template.

**Word tracks**
- “Here's what to expect as you drive. At this mileage, the fluids. At this mileage, the brakes. At this mileage, the major service. Keep this card in the glove box — we'll be ready for every one of them.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Frame the problem: the expectation gap behind sticker shock
- 3:00 – Build the card as a team from the manufacturer schedule (top models)
- 12:00 – Model the three-minute card delivery
- 15:00 – Pair drill: every advisor delivers the card twice
- 22:00 – Standard: every high-line delivery leaves with a card

**Your move**
Build the card for your top model. Every delivery gets one, starting Monday. *Academy: SMA 220 Why Customers Say Yes (weeks 21–24); revisited in SMA 330*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/5-15 mins/Active Delivery Audit — Pull Five ROs
title: Active Delivery Audit — Pull Five ROs
workbook_title: Active Delivery Audit — Pull Five ROs
best_used_for: Once a week, one-on-one with each advisor. Early in the week, so you have days left to coach the gaps.
body_md:
**Bring**
Five ROs from this week for that advisor, pulled by you.

**Word tracks**
- “This isn't a gotcha. I'm finding where I can help. Let's see what the five tell us.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Lay out five ROs; set the tone (not a gotcha)
- 1:00 – Walk each RO through the five delivery questions
- 8:00 – Mark the 25 boxes yes/no
- 10:00 – Circle the question with the most 'no' answers — that's this week's coaching focus
- 12:00 – Set next week's five-RO pull date

**Your move**
Pull five ROs for every advisor by Tuesday. Coach the circled box all week. Pull five more next Monday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/5-15 mins/Preview Two Intervals — Teach Advisors to Plan Ahead
title: Preview Two Intervals — Teach Advisors to Plan Ahead
workbook_title: Preview Two Intervals — Teach Advisors to Plan Ahead
best_used_for: Your active deliveries are ending at "you're all set," and your return rate isn't where it should be.
body_md:
**Bring**
Five fictitious ROs (vehicle, mileage, service history) and your interval chart.

**Word tracks**
- “Preview two intervals for me. Go.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Share the two-interval idea and why it protects CSI
- 2:00 – Drill: fictitious RO, 30 seconds to preview two intervals
- 8:00 – Note who needs interval-chart coaching
- 9:00 – Standard: every delivery previews two intervals; three listening checks per advisor

**Your move**
Build five fictitious ROs tonight. Run the drill every week until every advisor can do it without the chart.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/5-15 mins/Set Up the Tire Maintenance Ladder at Every Active Delivery
title: Set Up the Tire Maintenance Ladder at Every Active Delivery
workbook_title: Set Up the Tire Maintenance Ladder at Every Active Delivery
best_used_for: Your retention is soft, or your advisors deliver the vehicle without ever mentioning the next visit.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard; your manufacturer's maintenance schedule for the other ladders.

**Word tracks**
- “Great job rotating your tires today. Next time, we're going to do a rotate and balance.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Draw the tire ladder
- 2:00 – Model the "great job, next time" lines
- 4:00 – Small groups build fluid, filter, shock, battery ladders
- 7:00 – Groups share; each advisor drills a line
- 9:00 – Standard: next rung noted on every RO

**Your move**
Pull five closed ROs a day. Look for the next-visit note. No note — quick coaching conversation.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/Under 5 mins/'Items We ARE Going to Take Care of Next Time' — Say It Three Times
title: 'Items We ARE Going to Take Care of Next Time' — Say It Three Times
workbook_title: 'Items We ARE Going to Take Care of Next Time' — Say It Three Times
best_used_for: At delivery, your advisors rush past the deferred items. Or they say "you might want to think about" — and the customer leaves thinking, "I said no."
body_md:
**Bring**
One RO with a couple of deferred items on it.

**Word tracks**
- “After the approved items, walk through the deferred items with this line: 'Those items we ARE going to take care of next time.'”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The line and why 'we' + future tense work
- 1:00 – The rule of three: MPI, RO review, the door
- 2:00 – Manager models with a real RO
- 2:45 – Paired drill; partner counts the three
- 4:00 – Announce listen-ins on deferred-item deliveries; close

**Your move**
Run this drill tomorrow with a real RO, and listen for three "next times" on every delivery with a deferred item.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/Under 5 mins/'That Was a Good Decision' — The Versatile Closer
title: 'That Was a Good Decision' — The Versatile Closer
workbook_title: 'That Was a Good Decision' — The Versatile Closer
best_used_for: Customers approve work — but they leave quiet. Second-guessing. Calling back later to question the bill.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing — a few customer profiles ready for the rapid-fire drill.

**Word tracks**
- “For every approved recommendation — every single one — you say, 'That was a good decision.'”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The rule: every approval gets 'That was a good decision'
- 0:45 – The two personality versions: belong vs. feel special
- 1:30 – Rapid-fire drill: manager calls a profile, advisor picks the version
- 3:30 – Set the standard; announce two listen-ins per advisor; close

**Inspect it**
Inspect it. Listen in on two deliveries per advisor this week. Count the approvals. Count the affirmations. They should match.

**Your move**
Run the drill at your next huddle, and listen for those four words on every approval through Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/Under 5 mins/Certified Technician Graded — Not Found (Active Delivery Version)
title: Certified Technician Graded — Not Found (Active Delivery Version)
workbook_title: Certified Technician Graded — Not Found (Active Delivery Version)
situation_tags: Active delivery|Language and word tracks|Technicians and the shop
best_used_for: You hear advisors at delivery saying "we marked" or "found" when they walk through the MPI.
body_md:
**Bring**
One completed MPI with the certified technician's name on it.

**Word tracks**
- “At delivery, we never say 'found' and we never say 'we marked.' We say: 'My certified technician Hector graded every item on your vehicle's inspection.'”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The swap: 'graded', never 'found' or 'we marked'
- 0:45 – The why: who gives grades? Teachers — experts
- 1:30 – Manager models the MPI walk-through with the technician's name and the green/yellow/red gloss
- 2:30 – Each advisor delivers the opening; correct 'found' on the spot
- 4:00 – Set the standard; announce three listen-ins; close

**Inspect it**
Inspect it. Stand near three deliveries this week. Listen for ONE word.

**Your move**
Run this drill at your next huddle with a real MPI and a real certified technician's name.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/Under 5 mins/Pay by Phone — Protect Your Delivery Time
title: Pay by Phone — Protect Your Delivery Time
workbook_title: Pay by Phone — Protect Your Delivery Time
best_used_for: Deliveries feel rushed. Advisors spend the customer's last minutes at the counter running a card — and never get to the next visit, the survey, or the family.
body_md:
**Bring**
A stopwatch (or your phone) and a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “Phone payment isn't about convenience. It's about time. Every minute you spend processing a card is a minute you're not talking about the next visit, the survey, their other vehicles, or their family.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The why: payment is the lowest-value use of delivery time
- 0:45 – Stopwatch: time one counter payment
- 1:30 – Room calls out what they'd do with that time; write it on the board
- 2:30 – Phone-payment word track drilled once each
- 4:00 – Set the standard; announce Friday paid-ahead check; close

**Inspect it**
Inspect it. At the end of the week, check how many ROs were paid ahead of arrival, by advisor.

**Your move**
Run this huddle Monday, and check the paid-ahead count by advisor on Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/Under 5 mins/Say Thank You at Least Once Per Minute
title: Say Thank You at Least Once Per Minute
workbook_title: Say Thank You at Least Once Per Minute
best_used_for: Deliveries are getting transactional. Fast. Efficient. Cold. Customers leave with a receipt and no reason to come back.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing — the team counts on their fingers.

**Word tracks**
- “During delivery, a minimum of one thank you per minute. If you spend seven minutes with the customer, that's seven thank yous.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Share the standard: one thank you per minute
- 0:45 – The four thank-yous list
- 1:30 – Manager models a 3-minute delivery; team counts
- 3:00 – Pairs run it; partner counts
- 4:30 – Announce one observed delivery per advisor this week; close

**Your move**
Run the counting drill tomorrow morning and catch every advisor's delivery by Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Active Delivery/Under 5 mins/Text 'Your Vehicle Is Ready — I Need 3 to 7 Minutes'
title: Text 'Your Vehicle Is Ready — I Need 3 to 7 Minutes'
workbook_title: Text 'Your Vehicle Is Ready — I Need 3 to 7 Minutes'
best_used_for: Customers walk in, head straight for the cashier, keys in hand, already gone. Your advisors never get the conversation.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your phone with three 'your car is ready' texts your advisors sent yesterday.

**Word tracks**
- “From now on, the ready text says: 'Your vehicle is ready. When you arrive, I need 3 to 7 minutes with you — I have some information to share.'”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Read one of yesterday's 'your car is ready' texts out loud
- 0:45 – Share the new text and the three reasons it works
- 2:00 – Each advisor types and saves it as a template; show the room
- 3:30 – Set the standard; announce tomorrow's text check; close

**Inspect it**
Inspect it. Tomorrow, have each advisor show you their last three ready texts.

**Your move**
Run this before the drive opens, and check the texts at lunch tomorrow.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Building and Keeping the Team/15 plus mins/Hiring — Interview for the Walk-Around
title: Hiring — Interview for the Walk-Around
best_used_for: Before you post an advisor opening, and before every interview.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your top three advisors' habits on one page. A tread gauge and a car on the drive for the interview.

**Run sheet**
- Before posting (15 min): your best three advisors' daily habits on one page
- Call HR: what you can and can't ask
- Interview part ONE (15 min): story questions; listen for ownership
- Part TWO (10 min): walk a car together with a tread gauge
- Part THREE (5 min): the honest preview of the hard parts
- Same day: score every candidate on the same sheet

**Your move**
Write your best advisors' habits on one page before your next opening. *Academy: SMA 301 Building the Team (weeks 25–27); revisited in SMA 320*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Building and Keeping the Team/5-15 mins/Day 30 — The First Real Review
title: Day 30 — The First Real Review
best_used_for: Day 30 for every new advisor. Put it on the calendar the day they start.
body_md:
**Bring**
The new advisor's first 30 days of ROs, their coaching tier, and three specific moments you saw.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Ask first: 'How do you think the first month went?'
- 3:00 – Two specific positives, with the moment
- 5:00 – Name the coaching tier with evidence
- 7:00 – The ONE next step
- 9:00 – 'What do you need from me?' Write it down
- 11:00 – Set the Day 60 date together

**Your move**
Put Day 30 on the calendar for every advisor you've hired this year, even the ones past it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Building and Keeping the Team/5-15 mins/Losing an Advisor — Cover the Book, Hold the Team
title: Losing an Advisor — Cover the Book, Hold the Team
workbook_title: Losing an Advisor — Cover the Book, Hold the Team
situation_tags: Team culture|Morale and recognition|Standards and process
best_used_for: The morning after any advisor gives notice. Not a week later.
body_md:
**Bring**
The departing advisor's open ROs, deferred work, and appointments, split into a coverage plan.

**Word tracks**
- “You've heard. Friday is her last day. I'm happy for her, and we're going to miss her.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name it plainly; no spin
- 3:00 – The coverage plan: every open RO, deferred item and appointment has a name
- 8:00 – Hear the room; answer what you know, carry what you don't
- 13:00 – ONE standard that doesn't drop
- 15:00 – The send-off, if they're leaving well

**Your move**
Build the coverage plan before the meeting, and say it plainly.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Building and Keeping the Team/5-15 mins/The Pay Plan Conversation — Explain It Until They Can Explain It Back
title: The Pay Plan Conversation — Explain It Until They Can Explain It Back
workbook_title: The Pay Plan Conversation — Explain It Until They Can Explain It Back
best_used_for: A new pay plan. A change to the current one. Or any time you hear a rumor about either.
body_md:
**Bring**
The pay plan on one page, in plain words. Three example months worked out on paper. Your HR contact's answers to the questions you expect.

**Word tracks**
- “I want to make sure I explained it well. Walk me through how you'd get paid in a great month.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – What's changing and what isn't; bad news first
- 3:00 – Walk three example months: slow, average, great
- 7:00 – Teach-back: each advisor explains it in their own words
- 10:00 – Questions; anything you don't know gets a Friday answer
- 13:00 – Standard: the same answer for everyone

**Your move**
Work the three example months on paper before you say a word to the team.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Building and Keeping the Team/5-15 mins/Week ONE — The New Advisor's First Five Days
title: Week ONE — The New Advisor's First Five Days
workbook_title: Week ONE — The New Advisor's First Five Days
best_used_for: The Friday before a new advisor starts. Then every morning of their first week.
body_md:
**Bring**
A one-page Week ONE plan with the new advisor's name, a buddy assigned, and five days of ONE skill each.

**Run sheet**
- Friday before: one-page plan; pick a buddy (most consistent, not top seller)
- Mon – System: logins, DMS, pre-write; shadow every walk-around
- Tue – Language: share, graded, photo or video, deferred
- Wed – Lead three walk-arounds with the buddy
- Thu – Morning in the shop with Hector; watch a full MPI
- Fri – Follow-up calls with the buddy listening
- Daily (10 min): 'What surprised you? What do you want to do again?'
- Friday close: specific positives, ONE thing to work on

**Inspect it**
Friday, the phone. They make the follow-up calls with the buddy listening.

**Your move**
Write the five-day plan and pick the buddy before your new advisor walks in.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Building and Keeping the Team/5-15 mins/When Two Advisors Collide — Conflict Without Sides
title: When Two Advisors Collide — Conflict Without Sides
workbook_title: When Two Advisors Collide — Conflict Without Sides
best_used_for: The first time two advisors' conflict spills onto the drive. Not the third.
body_md:
**Bring**
Two chairs, ONE table, and the specific moments you saw. Not what you heard.

**Word tracks**
- “I'm not here to decide who's right. I'm here because the drive needs both of you, and right now it's getting neither.”

**Run sheet**
- Separately (10 min each): 'Tell me what happened from your side'; listen, write it down
- Together (15 min): you at the end of the table; the rules; ONE thing each needs from the other
- Write the agreement; both names on it
- Team (1 min): 'It's handled. We're one team.'

**Your move**
If two people on your drive have stopped talking, have the separate conversations today.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Building and Keeping the Team/Under 5 mins/Attendance — The Standard Starts at 7:00
title: Attendance — The Standard Starts at 7:00
best_used_for: The second late arrival in a month. Not the fifth.
body_md:
**Bring**
The schedule, the attendance record for the last 30 days, and your store's attendance policy.

**Word tracks**
- “You were in at seven-ten on Tuesday and seven-fifteen today. The schedule says seven.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The facts: dates and times, no adjectives
- 1:00 – Ask what's going on; listen
- 2:00 – Circumstance: fix the schedule. Habit: restate the standard
- 3:30 – Document it: date, what was said, follow-up date
- 4:30 – Policy and HR decide next steps, not mood

**Your move**
Have the conversation the same day you see the second late arrival.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/15 plus mins/Run De-Escalation Role Plays — Be a Realistic Customer, Not the Meanest One
title: Run De-Escalation Role Plays — Be a Realistic Customer, Not the Meanest One
workbook_title: Run De-Escalation Role Plays — Be a Realistic Customer, Not the Meanest One
situation_tags: Upset customers|Phones and BDC|CSI and surveys
best_used_for: Your BDC or your advisors are getting rattled on everyday upset calls. Or your CSI comments keep saying "nobody called me back."
body_md:
**Bring**
Three written realistic scenarios (car not ready on time, missed callback, repair higher than expected) and a four-skill observer sheet.

**Word tracks**
- “I'm not going to be the meanest customer you've ever had. I'm going to be the one you get on a Tuesday. Let's see the four skills.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why realistic beats villain
- 2:00 – Set the three scenarios and the realistic customer
- 4:00 – Name the four skills on the board
- 6:00 – Groups of three: caller, advisor, observer; rotate through all scenarios
- 18:00 – Debrief each scenario: strongest skill, skipped skill
- 22:00 – Standard: every upset call ends with an action item and a callback time

**Your move**
Write your three scenarios tonight. Run it at your next meeting. Then spot check three upset-call follow-ups by Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/15 plus mins/The Sugar-Free Snacks Story — Inclusive Amenities Are CSI Gold
title: The Sugar-Free Snacks Story — Inclusive Amenities Are CSI Gold
workbook_title: The Sugar-Free Snacks Story — Inclusive Amenities Are CSI Gold
best_used_for: Once a quarter. Put it on the calendar.
body_md:
**Bring**
A clipboard or phone for the gap list; bring ONE advisor, your porter, and whoever stocks the lounge.

**Word tracks**
- “We're going to look at this room through somebody else's eyes. Who is this NOT serving?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Share the sugar-free snacks story
- 3:00 – Walk the lounge: 'Who is this NOT serving?'
- 6:00 – Go customer by customer: dietary, mobility, small child, nursing mother
- 14:00 – Write every gap as a condition
- 17:00 – Assign ONE owner and ONE date per gap

**Your move**
Put the lounge walk on the calendar. Then stock the sugar-free snacks before you even get there. *Academy: SMA 410 Warranty, Policy and Compliance (weeks 40–42); revisited in SMA 210*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/5-15 mins/Efficiency vs Efficacy — Checking Boxes vs Checking Them With a Plus
title: Efficiency vs Efficacy — Checking Boxes vs Checking Them With a Plus
workbook_title: Efficiency vs Efficacy — Checking Boxes vs Checking Them With a Plus
best_used_for: Your team is hitting every process metric — calls made, MPIs sent, times met — and your CSI is still mediocre.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard; a simple scoring sheet for update calls (on time / with the plus).

**Word tracks**
- “We're good at checking boxes. Starting today, we check them with a plus. The goal is always both.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Define efficiency vs. efficacy
- 2:00 – Model the update call, efficient vs. with a plus
- 5:00 – Pair drill, then switch
- 8:00 – Name the plus for ONE more daily task
- 10:00 – Standard: every update call gets the plus; three-call scoring

**Your move**
Listen to three update calls per advisor. Score two things: on time, and the plus. Share the scores one-on-one by Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/Under 5 mins/'More Perfect' — The Bad Day Survey Handle
title: 'More Perfect' — The Bad Day Survey Handle
workbook_title: 'More Perfect' — The Bad Day Survey Handle
best_used_for: Right after a rough week, or the morning after a heat case your team is still talking about.
body_md:
**Bring**
Three real rough visits from the last month (advisor names removed); a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “When a visit goes sideways, our instinct is to skip the survey talk. Starting today, we lean into it instead.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the hide-from-the-survey instinct
- 1:00 – Put the "more perfect" line on the board
- 2:00 – Drill it on three real rough visits
- 4:00 – Standard: every rough visit gets the talk

**Your move**
The minute you hear about a rough visit, find that advisor before the delivery and hand them the line.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/Under 5 mins/More People Fill Out Surveys After Bad Experiences — So Ask Everyone
title: More People Fill Out Surveys After Bad Experiences — So Ask Everyone
workbook_title: More People Fill Out Surveys After Bad Experiences — So Ask Everyone
best_used_for: Your CSI is soft and your advisors are cherry-picking who hears about the survey.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing. Optional: your latest CSI report.

**Word tracks**
- “In my experience, the customer who had a frustrating visit finds the survey on their own. So we're going to ask everyone. Every single customer.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Share the idea: unhappy customers find the survey on their own
- 1:00 – Give the ONE survey line; each advisor says it once
- 3:00 – The why: asking everyone balances the sample
- 4:00 – Standard: every customer; listening check per advisor this week

**Your move**
Run it tomorrow morning. Do your listening checks by Friday. Then share back what you heard with the team.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/Under 5 mins/Schedule Deliveries for Heat Cases — Protect the Relationship
title: Schedule Deliveries for Heat Cases — Protect the Relationship
workbook_title: Schedule Deliveries for Heat Cases — Protect the Relationship
best_used_for: A heat case just walked out angry — rushed to the cashier window, and nobody acknowledged what went wrong.
body_md:
**Bring**
Two heat-case ROs from this month (names removed); a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “If you suspect a customer is a heat case, don't wait for the cashier window. Schedule the delivery.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Define a heat case on the board
- 1:00 – Model the scheduled-delivery line
- 2:00 – What happens in the ten minutes
- 3:00 – Drill on two real heat cases
- 4:30 – Standard: heat cases named every morning and scheduled

**Your move**
Sit in on ONE scheduled heat-case delivery. Watch it. Coach it afterward.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/Under 5 mins/Share Your Survey Score — Build Credibility
title: Share Your Survey Score — Build Credibility
workbook_title: Share Your Survey Score — Build Credibility
best_used_for: Your team is asking for surveys with vague requests. "If you could give us a good score, that'd be great."
body_md:
**Bring**
A printout of each advisor's survey score for the last 30 days, plus a copy of the survey your customers actually receive.

**Word tracks**
- “Thirty-eight of my last forty-one customers gave me a perfect survey. I would love for you to be thirty-nine.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Hand out each advisor's 30-day score
- 1:00 – Model the streak line and the monthly-goal line
- 2:00 – Walk through what perfect looks like on your actual survey
- 3:00 – Pair drill with real numbers, then switch
- 4:30 – Standard: score posted Mondays, listen by Wednesday

**Your move**
Every Monday, put each advisor's current score on their workstation. Then listen for it on the drive by Wednesday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/Under 5 mins/Survey Talk — Eliminate All Doubt Words
title: Survey Talk — Eliminate All Doubt Words
workbook_title: Survey Talk — Eliminate All Doubt Words
situation_tags: CSI and surveys|Language and word tracks
best_used_for: Survey scores are sliding, or you just heard "you might get a survey" on your drive.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard and marker; each advisor's real current survey score.

**Word tracks**
- “These four words are banned on our drive starting right now. Might. Hopefully. Fifty-fifty. Maybe. Every one of them makes our survey sound optional.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Doubt words on the board, crossed out
- 1:00 – Model the assertive survey line
- 2:00 – Add each advisor's real score
- 3:00 – Round-robin drill; doubt word = start over
- 4:30 – Set the standard: three delivery spot checks a day

**Your move**
Ban the four words in tomorrow's huddle, and catch ONE advisor doing it right before Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/Under 5 mins/Text Customers About Lounge Amenities — Including the Gaps
title: Text Customers About Lounge Amenities — Including the Gaps
workbook_title: Text Customers About Lounge Amenities — Including the Gaps
best_used_for: Your waiters are complaining about the lounge, or your team treats waiting customers like they're invisible until the vehicle is done.
body_md:
**Bring**
A quick walk of your lounge right before the meeting: Wi-Fi password, snacks, TV, and what's missing.

**Word tracks**
- “I just walked our lounge. Here's what's in it today — and here's what isn't. You should know this before every waiter walks in.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Share today's lounge walk
- 1:00 – Teach the amenity text and the gap text
- 2:30 – Every advisor drafts both texts; read three aloud
- 4:00 – Standard: every waiter gets a text, daily lounge walk

**Your move**
Make the lounge walk part of your opening routine, and check five waiter ROs a day for the text.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/CSI and Upset Customers/Under 5 mins/The White Rag Trick — Survey Score Lift
title: The White Rag Trick — Survey Score Lift
workbook_title: The White Rag Trick — Survey Score Lift
best_used_for: Your survey scores are stuck, and your deliveries have turned into a hand-off at the cashier window.
body_md:
**Bring**
A stack of clean white rags, one per advisor; a vehicle in the delivery lane.

**Word tracks**
- “That's exactly what your customer thinks. This advisor cares so much that even a smudge on the mirror gets handled.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Silent demo at the delivery lane
- 1:00 – Debrief: what did the customer see?
- 2:00 – Three rules: after the door, no explaining, walk away
- 3:00 – Every advisor runs it; hand out rags
- 4:30 – Standard: three delivery spot checks a day

**Your move**
Spot check three deliveries a day. Rag in the pocket. Mirror wiped. Mouth shut.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/5-15 mins/The Lion and the Jackals — Know Your Domain, Correct Early
title: The Lion and the Jackals — Know Your Domain, Correct Early
workbook_title: The Lion and the Jackals — Know Your Domain, Correct Early
situation_tags: Underperformance or accountability|Team culture|Standards and process
best_used_for: Your advisors are apologizing for offering services. Or a standard has been slipping, and nobody has said a word.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE standard that has slipped, written in ONE sentence. A whiteboard. Optional: the lion clip, if your store has cleared the rights.

**Word tracks**
- “The customer's domain is the decision. Our domain is the offer. We don't apologize for offering. It's our responsibility.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two specific positives
- 1:00 – Whiteboard: advisor's domain is the offer, customer's domain is the decision
- 3:00 – Hunt the jackals: the room names the slips and apology phrases
- 6:00 – Own your part, then deliver the standard calmly with the inspection day
- 9:00 – Each advisor names ONE jackal to chase off this week
- 11:00 – Close: early correction, every time

**Your move**
Correct the ONE standard you named, at the first bite, every time you see it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/5-15 mins/The Train — Reset, Confront, Celebrate
title: The Train — Reset, Confront, Celebrate
best_used_for: A new initiative. A dip in CSI or attach rate. Or ONE advisor who knows the standard and is choosing not to meet it.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your direction in ONE sentence. For any one-on-one: three behaviors you personally saw, and ONE number to track.

**Run sheet**
- Team reset (5 min): direction in ONE sentence; 'I need to know who is on it'; every advisor commits out loud
- One-on-one (10 min): two positives; three behaviors you saw; ask and listen; coach it, or deliver the Train once; silence
- Getting on (10 min): acknowledge; three behaviors; ONE number; a date three weeks out
- Three weeks later: celebrate or revisit

**Your move**
Write your direction in ONE sentence, and get every hand up. *Academy: SMA 301 Building the Team (weeks 25–27); revisited in SMA 410*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/Under 5 mins/Press for Specificity — Don't Let Generic Answers Stand
title: Press for Specificity — Don't Let Generic Answers Stand
workbook_title: Press for Specificity — Don't Let Generic Answers Stand
best_used_for: Any team meeting, any one-on-one — the moment you hear an abstract answer.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing. A whiteboard helps.

**Word tracks**
- “Be specific. What does that actually look like in a write-up?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Ask one open question
- 1:00 – Listen for the abstract noun
- 1:30 – Press: 'Be specific. What does that look like in a write-up?'
- 3:00 – Write the specific answer on the board as a standard

**Your move**
Train your ear for the abstract nouns. Every time you hear one, press ONE more time.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/Under 5 mins/Team Leadership: The Coaching Break
title: Team Leadership: The Coaching Break
best_used_for: Any week. Five minutes, one-on-one. Whenever you see someone on your team who is one break away from a different career.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE specific observation of something they did well, and ONE stretch opportunity to offer.

**Word tracks**
- “I think you're ready for more. I want you to run tomorrow's huddle — and I'll be right there with you.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Share the specific thing you've seen them do well
- 1:00 – Offer the break (e.g., run tomorrow's huddle)
- 2:30 – Plan your support: prep before, debrief after
- 4:00 – Write down who, what, and the check-in date

**Your move**
Pick ONE person. Give them the break. Then coach them all the way through it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/Under 5 mins/The Reference-Back
title: The Reference-Back
best_used_for: Every one-on-one, from here on out. Thirty seconds. Every time.
body_md:
**Set**
ONE Word

**Bring**
A list on your phone of every advisor and their ONE word.

**Word tracks**
- “How is dependability showing up for you this week?”
- “What would dependability do with this customer?”
- “Dependability just closed a big RO. That's who you are.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Open the one-on-one with their word
- 0:30 – Use the line that fits: check-in, tough stretch, or win
- 1:30 – Continue the regular one-on-one
- 4:00 – Close by tying the next step back to their word

**Your move**
Open every one-on-one with their word. Every one. And the next time someone nails it, say the word out loud in front of the team.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/Under 5 mins/The Thirty-Second Coaching Session
title: The Thirty-Second Coaching Session
best_used_for: You've got an advisor at elite tier. Fully engaged. Offering everything. Customers leaving happy.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing. Just eyes on the drive so you catch them in the act.

**Word tracks**
- “I watched what you did with that customer. I'm not going to change anything. Keep doing exactly that.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Observe the advisor with a real customer
- 0:10 – Walk up, eye contact, deliver the line word for word
- 0:25 – Walk away: no follow-up, no suggestion, no plan
- Afterward – Protect the space; do not circle back to add coaching

**Your move**
Find ONE advisor who's crushing it. Thirty seconds. Then get out of the way.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/Under 5 mins/This Too Shall Pass — In Both Directions
title: This Too Shall Pass — In Both Directions
workbook_title: This Too Shall Pass — In Both Directions
best_used_for: Before any coaching conversation — when an advisor is at the bottom, or when they're at the top.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing.

**Word tracks**
- “Enjoy this. You earned it. And remember — this too shall pass. The conditions that made this month easy will shift. Keep the habits. The habits are what got you here.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Sit down; read the moment (rough week or streak)
- 0:15 – Deliver "This too shall pass" in the right tone
- 0:45 – Struggling: coach ONE thing for tomorrow / Streak: name the habits to keep
- 2:00 – Close with a handshake and a next step

**Your move**
Find ONE advisor at the bottom and ONE at the top. Same four words. Watch what happens to both conversations.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/Under 5 mins/Two Positives Before Any Negative — The Mentor Meeting Structure
title: Two Positives Before Any Negative — The Mentor Meeting Structure
workbook_title: Two Positives Before Any Negative — The Mentor Meeting Structure
best_used_for: Any feedback conversation. A tech meeting. A BDC review. A one-on-one with an advisor.
body_md:
**Bring**
Their numbers, plus two specific, recent positives written down before you walk in.

**Word tracks**
- “Hector, your video MPI completion rate has been great. The cabin air filter photos you've been taking are strong. However, our time-and-mileage recommendations are down. Here's what I suggest.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Positive number one (specific, earned)
- 0:45 – Positive number two (specific, recent)
- 1:30 – The gap and your suggestion
- 3:00 – Agree on ONE next step and the date you'll check it

**Your move**
Before your next tough conversation, write the two positives down first. Then walk in.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coaching and Accountability/Under 5 mins/We Fail Together — But Success Belongs to the Individual
title: We Fail Together — But Success Belongs to the Individual
workbook_title: We Fail Together — But Success Belongs to the Individual
best_used_for: Open any accountability conversation with it. A missed month. A rough survey. A campaign that fell flat.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing — just the standard, the miss you're owning, and ONE advisor win to name.

**Word tracks**
- “We fail together. But success needs to be enjoyed by the individual. When we miss, we miss as a team. When you win, the win is yours.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – State the standard out loud (both halves)
- 0:45 – Own the loss: name the miss, take your share first
- 1:30 – Give away the win: name ONE advisor and the specific behavior
- 2:00 – Move into the rest of the meeting

**Your move**
Next time a number misses, say "we." Next time someone wins, say their name.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Contests/5-15 mins/Celebrate Wins — Gamify the Right Metrics
title: Celebrate Wins — Gamify the Right Metrics
workbook_title: Celebrate Wins — Gamify the Right Metrics
best_used_for: The team's grinding. Nobody's smiling. Every meeting has been about what went wrong.
body_md:
**Bring**
A gift card for the word-track winner, a whiteboard with reservations set, reservations kept, and show-up percentage by name.

**Word tracks**
- “I want to hear one moment this week where your words made the difference. Best story takes the prize.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Open: why celebrating wins is a retention tool
- 1:00 – Word track of the day: each person shares one call moment (30 seconds each)
- 6:00 – Team vote; award the gift card
- 8:00 – Scoreboard: reservations set, reservations kept, show-up percentage; record drawing and fun-word points
- 11:00 – Pick the metric for next week; close

**Your move**
Pick ONE metric, put it on the board Monday, and open Friday's meeting with word track of the day.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Contests/5-15 mins/Contest — Golf Score
title: Contest — Golf Score
best_used_for: Any month you want the whole team in the race.
body_md:
**Bring**
A board or sheet with the three categories, last period's baselines for each advisor, the special-emphasis item, and the posted tiebreaker.

**Word tracks**
- “Top producer or brand new — everybody's got a shot. Win a category, place in the others, and you're in it.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The pitfall story: growth-only and totals-only contests
- 2:00 – Announce the three categories and the special-emphasis item
- 4:00 – Walk the scoring with an example: add placings, lowest wins
- 6:00 – Post the tiebreaker (total gross increase) and the contest dates
- 8:00 – Commit: standings on the board every morning

**Your move**
Pick your three categories, post the tiebreaker, and put the standings on the board every morning.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Contests/5-15 mins/Five-Category Fuel Sales Contest
title: Five-Category Fuel Sales Contest
best_used_for: Fuel services are soft. Or one advisor is carrying the whole category while everybody else watches.
body_md:
**Bring**
Last week's fuel sales by advisor for fuel injector clean (FIC-045), decarb service (FIC-046), throttle body clean (TBC-044), tank additive (FIC-047), and overall fuel; a five-column board.

**Word tracks**
- “Five categories this week. Injectors, decarb, throttle body, tank additive, and overall fuel. Five winners on Friday. Pick your category and go get it.”

**Run sheet**
- Mon 0:00 – Launch: share the five categories and the one-week window
- Mon 3:00 – Point advisors at tank additive as the first-yes building block; post the five-column board
- Daily – Update the board; read it at the morning huddle
- Fri 0:00 – Recognition meeting: name the winner in each of the five categories
- Fri 5:00 – Name the patterns and flag category gaps for next week's one-on-ones
- Fri 10:00 – Close; set next week's focus

**Your move**
Pull last week's fuel numbers by advisor, build the five-column board, and launch it Monday morning.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Contests/5-15 mins/Gamify the Metric You Want to Move
title: Gamify the Metric You Want to Move
workbook_title: Gamify the Metric You Want to Move
best_used_for: You've got ONE metric that's stuck. You've talked about it. You've reminded people. Nothing's moved.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your reports to identify the metric that needs the most movement, a whiteboard, a small daily reward, and a larger two-week champion reward.

**Word tracks**
- “For the next two weeks, this is the number. It's going on the board, every day, by name. Daily leader gets something small. Two-week champion gets something bigger.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the stuck metric and why it matters
- 2:00 – Share the rules: two weeks, daily leader reward, champion reward
- 4:00 – Post the board; show today's starting numbers by name
- Daily – Morning update and daily-leader reward
- Day 14 – Crown the champion in front of the team; keep the number posted one more week

**Your move**
Pull your reports, find the number that needs the most movement, and put it on the board Monday morning.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Contests/5-15 mins/Swing for the Fences — Fast Finish Contest
title: Swing for the Fences — Fast Finish Contest
workbook_title: Swing for the Fences — Fast Finish Contest
best_used_for: The last ten days or so. Any items you want focused. Change the lineup month to month.
body_md:
**Bring**
A printed lineup card (singles, doubles, triples, home runs) with your chosen items (include the dollar threshold for a collision-center referral); a scoreboard; the prizes.

**Word tracks**
- “Swing for the fences and earn great prizes. Every item you sell this month counts toward your contest numbers. The more you offer, the more you'll sell. The more you sell, the more chances you have to win big.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Frame: fast finish, everyone can win
- 2:00 – Walk the lineup card: singles 1, doubles 2, triples 3, home runs 5
- 6:00 – The pitch (Say this)
- 8:00 – Scoreboard posted, updated daily
- 10:00 – Round the room: ONE play each; send-off line

**Your move**
Build your own lineup: your singles, doubles, triples and home runs. Launch it at tomorrow's huddle. *Academy: SMA 110 The Daily Huddle (weeks 5–8); revisited in SMA 220*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Contests/5-15 mins/The Ten and Five Contest — Reward the Most NOs
title: The Ten and Five Contest — Reward the Most NOs
workbook_title: The Ten and Five Contest — Reward the Most NOs
best_used_for: Pick ONE day that normally has good traffic. Everybody gets a fair shot.
body_md:
**Bring**
Breakfast, cash for payouts (or the accounting form), yes/no tally sheets for each advisor, and your chosen featured services.

**Word tracks**
- “From now until 11:00 — ONE day only — every featured service you sell pays $10. Every ticket where you offer it and the customer says no pays $5. Whoever gets told no the most gets $25. Track your yeses and your nos. I'll be on the drive listening for our word tracks.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Breakfast and the announcement: $10 per featured service sold, $5 per no, $25 for the most nos
- 3:00 – Sell the mindset: .300 hitters, the quality no, 30% closing is great
- 6:00 – Hand out tally sheets; sandbagging warning
- 7:00–11:00 a.m. – Contest runs; manager walks the drive listening for word tracks
- 11:01 – Pay out and collect the objections advisors heard

**Your move**
Pick your day, pick your featured services, and bring breakfast.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Contests/5-15 mins/Three-Tier Contest — Something New, Something Forgotten, CSI
title: Three-Tier Contest — Something New, Something Forgotten, CSI
workbook_title: Three-Tier Contest — Something New, Something Forgotten, CSI
situation_tags: Start of month|Contests|Product knowledge and launches
best_used_for: Early in the month, when you've got a new service to launch and an old one gathering dust.
body_md:
**Bring**
Contest sheet with the three categories; your chosen new item and forgotten items; each advisor's CSI target; a standings board.

**Word tracks**
- “Here's an example. ONE advisor's CSI target is 8.7 and they finish at 9.4. That's an 8% boost. Their new-item and tire total goes up 8%.”
- “I'll post standings, but I don't want you waiting on me. Track your own. Your goals have to be measurable, trackable and attainable.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why three tiers: new, forgotten, CSI
- 2:00 – Name the categories for this contest period
- 4:00 – Scoring: rank on gross; CSI multiplier; walk the CSI multiplier example
- 8:00 – Self-tracking: measurable, trackable, attainable; watch for zeros
- 11:00 – Scoreboard speech; launch date and weekly standings

**Your move**
Pick your new item and your forgotten items. Set every advisor's CSI target. Launch it Monday, with standings posted every Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coverage Is Key/5-15 mins/Track Your Coverage Is Key Tier Mix
title: Track Your Coverage Is Key Tier Mix
workbook_title: Track Your Coverage Is Key Tier Mix
situation_tags: Coverage Is Key|Attach rate or ticket flat
best_used_for: Once a month. Or when covered-service authorizations look flat and you can't see why.
body_md:
**Bring**
Covered-service authorizations for the month by advisor, bucketed by mileage at write- up around your program's mileage cutoff (well before it, the window just before it, past it); one real RO from the just-before-the-cutoff bucket.

**Word tracks**
- “A customer just before the cutoff is in a different spot than a customer well past it. The pitch should sound different. Let's look at how we're doing it.”

**Run sheet**
- Solo 0:00 – Pull authorizations by advisor; bucket well before the cutoff / just before it / past it
- Solo 5:00 – Read the mix: is the just-before-the-cutoff window getting the urgency close?
- Team 0:00 – Two positives; show the buckets by advisor
- Team 4:00 – Drill the urgency close on one real RO from the window
- Team 9:00 – Set the target; announce the two-week report rerun; close

**Inspect it**
Inspect it. Rerun the report in two weeks. Same buckets. Same advisors.

**Your move**
Here's your move this month. Build the three-bucket report this week and run this meeting before month end. *Academy: SMA 330 The Shop Partnership (weeks 34–36); revisited in SMA 420*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coverage Is Key/Under 5 mins/Coverage Is Key Share
title: Coverage Is Key Share
best_used_for: Any morning. Especially the mornings when Coverage Is Key hasn't come up in a while.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing.

**Word tracks**
- “Today is a great day to share Coverage Is Key. In a video, during a presentation, or at delivery. Don't keep it a secret.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Gather advisors and certified technicians; share the 'don't keep it a secret' line
- 0:45 – Walk the three places: video, presentation, delivery
- 2:00 – Each person names the one spot they'll own today
- 3:00 – Close; end-of-day story collection, celebrated at tomorrow's huddle

**Your move**
Run this huddle before the first appointment, then collect one Coverage Is Key story by closing time.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coverage Is Key/Under 5 mins/Disclose the Waiting Period Up Front
title: Disclose the Waiting Period Up Front
workbook_title: Disclose the Waiting Period Up Front
best_used_for: Advisors are closing covered services and the waiting period isn't coming up. Or you've already had one upset customer and you don't want a second.
body_md:
**Bring**
One RO with a warranty-covered service for the role play.

**Word tracks**
- “The waiting period is part of the coverage. We share it with every customer, every time, before they leave. A surprise later costs us more than a sentence now.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The why: the claim-in-the-waiting-period story
- 1:00 – Manager models the disclosure line
- 1:45 – Paired role play, then switch
- 3:45 – Set the standard (shared and noted on the RO); announce Friday RO pull
- 4:30 – Close

**Inspect it**
Inspect it. Pull five covered ROs on Friday. If the note isn't there, that's a one-on-one.

**Your move**
Run the role play at tomorrow's huddle and check five covered ROs by Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coverage Is Key/Under 5 mins/Every Covered Service RO Includes the Coverage Is Key Close
title: Every Covered Service RO Includes the Coverage Is Key Close
workbook_title: Every Covered Service RO Includes the Coverage Is Key Close
best_used_for: You're pulling ROs and you see covered services sold — but nothing on the RO, the video, or the delivery notes shows the customer heard about Coverage Is Key.
body_md:
**Bring**
Three or four of yesterday's ROs with warranty-covered services on them.

**Word tracks**
- “Coverage Is Key is our signature differentiator. Every customer who pays for a covered service should leave knowing they got coverage. Every single one.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The why: the coverage is the signature differentiator
- 0:45 – Manager models the Coverage Is Key close
- 1:30 – Each advisor says their version once
- 3:30 – Set the standard and announce the daily five-RO spot check
- 4:30 – Close

**Inspect it**
And let them know how you'll inspect it. Tomorrow you pull five covered ROs at random and ask the advisor ONE question: did this customer hear about their coverage?

**Your move**
Run this huddle tomorrow morning, then spot-check five covered ROs every day through Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coverage Is Key/Under 5 mins/Talk Up Coverage Is Key — Proactively, Every Visit
title: Talk Up Coverage Is Key — Proactively, Every Visit
workbook_title: Talk Up Coverage Is Key — Proactively, Every Visit
best_used_for: Exchange volume is healthy, claims are low, and your returning customers have no idea what's covered.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your fluid exchange volume and warranty claims for the last month, plus the list of services that carry your warranty.

**Word tracks**
- “Every covered service gets the coverage line at delivery. Eight seconds. No exceptions.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The two numbers: exchange volume vs. coverage claims
- 1:00 – The eight-second coverage line
- 2:00 – Name every covered service
- 3:00 – Around the room: each advisor delivers the line once
- 4:30 – Standard and listening check

**Your move**
Run the huddle tomorrow. Do your listening checks by Friday. Then compare next month's claims to this month's.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Coverage Is Key/Under 5 mins/Verify Eligibility Out Loud
title: Verify Eligibility Out Loud
best_used_for: You catch an advisor pitching the Coverage Is Key close to a customer who doesn't qualify. Or you want to get ahead of it before it happens.
body_md:
**Bring**
An eligibility card for each advisor with the current program's mileage, age, and use limits.

**Word tracks**
- “Pitching coverage to someone who doesn't qualify wastes your pitch. Worse — when they find out later, you lose credibility. We verify eligibility out loud, every time.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The why: wasted pitch and lost credibility
- 0:45 – Manager models the out-loud eligibility check
- 1:30 – Three-scenario drill around the room
- 3:30 – Set the standard; announce three listen-ins per advisor this week
- 4:30 – Close; hand out eligibility cards

**Inspect it**
Then — model it. Out loud means the customer hears you check. Inspect it. This week, listen in on three deliveries per advisor. Did you hear the check?

**Your move**
Print the eligibility card, put one at every advisor's desk, and run this huddle before the drive opens tomorrow.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/5-15 mins/'Are You Familiar' — Drill It Until It Is Natural
title: 'Are You Familiar' — Drill It Until It Is Natural
workbook_title: 'Are You Familiar' — Drill It Until It Is Natural
situation_tags: New hire or onboarding|Language and word tracks
best_used_for: New advisor training. And the opening five minutes of any weekly team meeting.
body_md:
**Bring**
A list of your services.

**Word tracks**
- “I don't care if it sounds stiff right now. By the tenth time, it'll sound like you've been saying it for years.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Model it: manager says the line on three services
- 1:00 – Lap one: one service, every advisor says it to the person next to them
- 3:00 – Laps two and three on new services, fast pace
- 5:00 – Set the standard (every customer hears it once) and how you'll inspect it on the drive
- 6:00 – Move into the rest of the meeting

**Inspect it**
Inspect it. Walk the drive. Listen for it. When you hear it, catch them doing it right, out loud.

**Your move**
Open your next three team meetings with this drill. Different service each time.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/5-15 mins/Let Advisors Find Their Low-Key Word
title: Let Advisors Find Their Low-Key Word
workbook_title: Let Advisors Find Their Low-Key Word
situation_tags: New hire or onboarding|Language and word tracks
best_used_for: New-hire coaching. Or anytime an advisor pushes back on a word track.
body_md:
**Bring**
The word track the advisor is resisting, and a pen to write down their version.

**Word tracks**
- “Which word in there doesn't feel like you?”
- “That's yours now. Keep the structure. Own the words inside it.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Advisor delivers the word track; listen for the stiff word
- 2:00 – Ask which word doesn't feel like them; identify what the word is doing
- 4:00 – Find their version together; lock the structure (steps, order, photo or video)
- 7:00 – Advisor runs it three times with their word; write it down
- 9:00 – Close: their word track gets inspected like anyone else's

**Inspect it**
Write their word down. It's their word track now. Inspect it the same way you'd inspect anybody else's.

**Your move**
Sit with ONE advisor who sounds stiff. Find the ONE word. Help them make it theirs.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/5-15 mins/Trendy Words
title: Trendy Words
best_used_for: Once a quarter. Or anytime your team and your younger customers are talking past each other.
body_md:
**Bring**
A fresh list of five or six trending slang words, searched the morning of the meeting.

**Word tracks**
- “We're not learning these to use them. We're learning them so we understand what our customers mean. When a customer says your walkaround ate, that's a compliment. Take the W.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Open: why customer language matters; put five or six words up, undefined
- 2:00 – Go around the room: team guesses meanings and shares where they've heard them
- 5:00 – Reveal meanings (youngest advisor holds the answer key)
- 7:00 – Connect to the drive: understand, don't imitate; read the 'Say this' line
- 9:00 – Close: set the next refresh date

**Your move**
Pull a fresh list. Ten minutes at the start of your next team meeting. Let your youngest advisor hold the answer key.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/5-15 mins/Two Analogies, Not One
title: Two Analogies, Not One
situation_tags: Language and word tracks|Attach rate or ticket flat
best_used_for: Your team's word tracks sound memorized — and close rates are flat.
body_md:
**Bring**
The two fuel system word tracks (sore throat and clogged artery), printed side by side.

**Word tracks**
- “You're not memorizing a script. You're carrying two tools. Read the person in front of you, then pick.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The one-script mistake
- 2:00 – Model method one: sore throat
- 4:00 – Model method two: clogged artery
- 6:00 – Who each one fits
- 8:00 – Pairs drill: read the customer, pick the tool, deliver it
- 12:00 – Standard: every advisor ready with BOTH

**Your move**
ask every advisor to share both fuel system analogies with you, cold. Anyone who can only do ONE gets a second rep before Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/5-15 mins/Vocabulary Meeting
title: Vocabulary Meeting
situation_tags: Mid-month|Language and word tracks|Morale and recognition
best_used_for: Mid-month. Or any time the energy on your drive feels flat.
body_md:
**Bring**
A printed word-swap card for each desk and your list of the four or five models that cross your drive most.

**Word tracks**
- “How may I serve you today?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The greeting: an enthusiastic 'Welcome!' for ALL customers
- 2:00 – Serve, not help; 'My pleasure,' not 'you're welcome'
- 4:00 – Rapid-fire word swap list
- 8:00 – Feel, Felt, Found once around the room
- 10:00 – Top four or five models and their hot features

**Your move**
Put the swap card on every desk and listen for "serve" and "my pleasure" on every write-up.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/5-15 mins/Word Track of the Day — Team Contest
title: Word Track of the Day — Team Contest
workbook_title: Word Track of the Day — Team Contest
best_used_for: Your team knows the language. They nailed it in class. But you're still hearing "issue" on the drive and "tell" on the phone.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE gift card to a local restaurant and a short list of the target phrases.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Launch: name the target phrases and the prize
- 1:00 – Each advisor shares ONE real word track story (60 seconds max)
- 9:00 – Team vote by show of hands
- 10:00 – Award the gift card in front of the team

**Your move**
Announce it tomorrow morning. Buy ONE gift card. First vote is Friday. *Academy: SMA 220 Why Customers Say Yes (weeks 21–24); revisited in SMA 210*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/Under 5 mins/"That's Our Policy" — Never Say This
title: "That's Our Policy" — Never Say This
best_used_for: You heard it at the counter. Or on the phone. Or you read it in a survey comment.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard; three quick customer scenarios where the answer is no.

**Word tracks**
- “From today, we don't hide behind policy. When the answer is no, you lead with what you CAN do. Every time.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the phrase and what customers hear
- 1:00 – Give the replacement line
- 2:00 – Role-play three 'no' scenarios with the replacement
- 4:00 – Retire the phrase; coach it on the spot when heard

**Your move**
Listen for the phrase at the counter. When you catch it, pull that advisor aside and rehearse the replacement line together — once.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/Under 5 mins/"We Can't Do That" → "Here's What We Can Do Right Now"
title: "We Can't Do That" → "Here's What We Can Do Right Now"
workbook_title: "We Can't Do That" → "Here's What We Can Do Right Now"
best_used_for: You're hearing "can't" at the counter. Or customers are escalating to you when they didn't need to.
body_md:
**Bring**
A hand-off list: the name of the go-to person for parts, warranty, finance and the shop.

**Word tracks**
- “We're done closing doors. When your options are limited, you name the action you CAN take. That's what moves a customer from stuck to helped.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the closed door and the replacement line
- 1:00 – Teach the hand-off by name
- 2:00 – Rapid-fire drill: manager throws requests, advisors answer with what they can do
- 4:00 – Set the standard: names, not departments; post the hand-off list

**Your move**
Post the hand-off list at every desk. Then catch ONE advisor turning a "can't" into a "can" — and recognize it in front of the team.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Language and Word Tracks/Under 5 mins/How Many Times Has a Customer Been to a Service Department
title: How Many Times Has a Customer Been to a Service Department
workbook_title: How Many Times Has a Customer Been to a Service Department
best_used_for: Morning huddle. Especially when the drive starts sounding like a recording.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing — just the math.

**Word tracks**
- “You might write up fifteen customers today. Your customer has been to a service department maybe twenty times in their whole life. In ONE day, you'll have nearly as many as they've had — ever.”
- “Talk to every customer as if it's their very first time at a dealership. Every time.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The math: 15 write-ups today vs. ~20 lifetime visits
- 1:00 – Name the trap: complacency from repetition
- 2:00 – Set the standard: every customer's first time
- 3:00 – Open the doors

**Your move**
Today, listen for ONE advisor who sounds like a recording. Pull them aside after the write-up and reset them with the math.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/15 plus mins/Books, Body Language, Bro-Speak (Solo)
title: Books, Body Language, Bro-Speak (Solo)
best_used_for: A Saturday. Coffee. No phones ringing. Your own time.
body_md:
**Bring**
A notebook, an hour or more of quiet time, and a book choice (or a day of people- watching).

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Reflect: what's going well, what's a struggle (notebook)
- 15:00 – Option 1: pick a book, pull tidbits for the team
- Rest of day – Option 2: body language experiment (walk faster, point, observe reactions)
- Any time – Option 3: research new communication (Bro-Speak) or something bigger
- End of day – Write ONE tidbit for Monday's huddle

**Your move**
Here's your move this weekend. Pick your book. Write down ONE tidbit to share at Monday's huddle.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/15 plus mins/Diagnose the Level Before You Prescribe the Coaching
title: Diagnose the Level Before You Prescribe the Coaching
workbook_title: Diagnose the Level Before You Prescribe the Coaching
best_used_for: Any time a number won't move. Before you schedule one more class.
body_md:
**Bring**
The attach rate report for the stuck service, by advisor, and a page to record each advisor's level.

**Word tracks**
- “Walk me through why a customer needs this — like I'm the customer.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Pull the attach rate report; list advisors
- 2:00 – Advisor 1: explain it / last successful offer / what changed — record the level
- 7:00 – Repeat for each advisor (~5 minutes each)
- 25:00 – Group advisors by level; match each level to its coaching move
- 30:00 – Development plan set; schedule follow-ups

**Your move**
Before the next class, run the three questions with every advisor. Write their level next to their name.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/15 plus mins/Succession Plan
title: Succession Plan
best_used_for: Twice a year. Before a vacation. Anytime you've added people or lost people.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your current roster, a blank sheet for the org chart, and an hour with the door closed; then a test week on the calendar.

**Word tracks**
- “I'm handing you this because I trust you. I'll be right here. Let's see what you can do.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Draw the organizational chart: every name, every seat
- 15:00 – Person by person: strengths, right seat today, where they're headed
- 35:00 – Build the succession plan for a one-to-two-week absence (including assistant / drive manager coverage)
- 50:00 – Pick the test week and put it on the calendar
- Test week – 'Miss' the week: shadow, coach rough patches, reinforce that each person matters

**Your move**
Block one hour. Draw the chart. Then put your test week on the calendar.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/15 plus mins/The Value Scavenger Hunt
title: The Value Scavenger Hunt
best_used_for: A weekend. A slow Sunday. Any day you've got room to think instead of react.
body_md:
**Bring**
A notebook or phone notes; your Service Manager Journal.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Write your own definition of value; read the dictionary definition
- 0:10 – Break it down: importance and worth, usefulness and benefit, high opinion
- 0:20 – Go hunt: visit places you'd normally visit and log every moment of unexpected value
- End of day – Journal what you found and pick the ONE idea that fits your drive
- Monday – Bring that idea to your team meeting

**Your move**
Here's your move this weekend. Write down what value means to you. Find three examples of it out in the world. Bring the best ONE to your Monday meeting. *Academy: SMA 310 Coaching Advisors (weeks 28–30); revisited in SMA 301*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/15 plus mins/Two Crappy Pages a Day — The Manager Observation Journal
title: Two Crappy Pages a Day — The Manager Observation Journal
workbook_title: Two Crappy Pages a Day — The Manager Observation Journal
best_used_for: Every day — and once a month, for real.
body_md:
**Bring**
A notebook or phone notes app that travels with you; for the monthly session, the month's notes and 30–45 blocked minutes.

**Run sheet**
- Daily, 0:00 – Walk the drive, listen to calls, watch write-ups
- Daily, all shift – Capture two or three observations in your notebook or phone
- Monthly, 0:00 – Block 30–45 minutes, door closed; reread the month's notes
- Monthly, 10:00 – Write 500 words: direction, cracks, wins, adjustments
- Monthly, 35:00 – Circle ONE adjustment to act on next month

**Your move**
Grab a notebook. Write down three things you saw on the drive before you go home.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/15 plus mins/Wow Factor — The Solo Field Trip
title: Wow Factor — The Solo Field Trip
workbook_title: Wow Factor — The Solo Field Trip
best_used_for: A weekend. Your own time. With someone whose opinion you trust.
body_md:
**Bring**
A friend or family member, a reservation at a restaurant or event, and the five-item watch list on your phone.

**Run sheet**
- Before – Share the five-item watch list with your guest
- During (60–90 min) – Note response time, extras, communication, gratitude, personality
- After (15 min) – Debrief with your guest: what fits their world, what fits yours
- Monday – Pick ONE detail your team will copy and start it that week

**Your move**
Here's your move this weekend. Book the table. Bring a guest. Come back Monday with ONE thing your team will copy, and start it that week.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/5-15 mins/Invest Deeply in Your Advisors
title: Invest Deeply in Your Advisors
best_used_for: Start of the month. Or the week you lose an advisor and wonder why.
body_md:
**Set**
Coaching Investment

**Bring**
A list of your advisors, your calendar, and last month's one-on-one notes.

**Word tracks**
- “This thirty minutes is yours. Every week. I'm invested in your success — so let's talk about what you want to win next.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – List every advisor down the page
- 3:00 – Score last month's real investment: one-on-ones, Ten and Five contest, objection playbook, workstation walks
- 9:00 – Identify the empty rows — your retention risks
- 12:00 – Block 30 minutes per advisor per week on the calendar; set a 30-day re-inspect date

**Your move**
Fill every empty row. Inspect the page again in thirty days.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/5-15 mins/Personal Development
title: Personal Development
best_used_for: A Saturday. A quiet morning. Any day you realize you've been pouring from an empty cup.
body_md:
**Bring**
A notebook and pen; your Service Manager Journal.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Choose ONE area to develop (Maslow's five needs or the alternate list)
- 2:00 – Take the first small step now: water, deep breaths, a walk, a volunteer call
- 5:00 – Write your 30-second impact speech
- 10:00 – Deliver it to yourself, emphasizing different words; journal the step you'll repeat
- Later – Give the speech to a close friend or loved one

**Your move**
Here's your move this weekend. Pick your ONE area, take ONE small step today, and write your 30-second speech before Monday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/5-15 mins/Positivity and Inspiration (Solo)
title: Positivity and Inspiration (Solo)
best_used_for: Sunday night, any week the grind starts to wear on you.
body_md:
**Bring**
A pen and paper; a quiet place, a walk, or scripture.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Write the list of positives from the week or month
- 4:00 – Motivation vs. inspiration: read the two definitions
- 6:00 – Go find inspiration: scripture, a walk, observation
- 11:00 – Self-check: coaching to 'act or behave' vs. to feel and DO
- 14:00 – Pick ONE positive to share at Monday's huddle

**Your move**
Take ONE thing from your list into Monday's huddle. Share it. Name the person. Then point the room at what they can do next.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/5-15 mins/Pressure, Not Manipulation — The Six Checks of Real Coaching
title: Pressure, Not Manipulation — The Six Checks of Real Coaching
workbook_title: Pressure, Not Manipulation — The Six Checks of Real Coaching
best_used_for: Before any tough one-on-one. Before you build a performance plan. Or with your management team, any time you raise the bar.
body_md:
**Bring**
A notepad. Every active performance plan and every new advisor's workload.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The ONE test: grow them, or build a case?
- 2:00 – The four-part line: standard, gap, need, consequence
- 4:00 – Audit every performance plan and new-advisor workload; fix anything built to be failed
- 9:00 – Before each one-on-one: the six checks
- After – Grade yourself; circle the misses
- This week – Celebrate ONE advisor who rose to a push

**Your move**
Rewrite ONE plan you wouldn't be proud to have your team read. And run the six checks before every one-on-one.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Leading Yourself/5-15 mins/Teach Mode vs. Preach Mode
title: Teach Mode vs. Preach Mode
best_used_for: Every training meeting you run.
body_md:
**Bring**
Whatever concept you're teaching this week, on a screen or whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “When the screen's up, I'm in teach mode. When it goes off, I'm in preach mode — and that's when I want to hear from you.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the two modes out loud
- 1:00 – Teach mode: what the concept is
- 4:00 – Preach mode: screen off, what it means to YOU
- 9:00 – Back to teach mode: how to apply it
- 12:00 – Close: one commitment per advisor

**Your move**
in your next team meeting, turn the screen off at least once — and let your advisors do the talking.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/15 plus mins/Cooling System Seasonal Campaign
title: Cooling System Seasonal Campaign
best_used_for: Twice a year. Spring — April or May. Fall — September or October.
body_md:
**Bring**
Campaign calendar, coolant exchange attach rate by advisor, and the cooling system menu.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why coolant needs a seasonal trigger
- 2:00 – Walk the campaign calendar: start, end, weekly audit days
- 5:00 – Teach the seasonal language: spring = overheating, fall = freeze protection
- 10:00 – Drill: every advisor says the seasonal line out loud twice
- 13:00 – Pair with the cooling system menu for full-system authorizations
- 16:00 – Set the weekly audit standard

**Inspect it**
Every week of the campaign, you check it. Are your advisors using the seasonal language? Is coolant graded on the MPI with a photo or video?

**Your move**
Here's your move this season. Mark the campaign on the calendar. Train the language. Audit it every week until the season turns.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/15 plus mins/Demo New Products in Your Own Car First
title: Demo New Products in Your Own Car First
workbook_title: Demo New Products in Your Own Car First
best_used_for: Before you launch any new service to your advisors. Before. Not after.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your product rep, ONE vehicle (yours or a dealership unit), and the product being launched.

**Word tracks**
- “In one sentence, share what you just experienced — the way you'd share it with a customer on the drive.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Rep performs the service on ONE vehicle in front of the team
- 5:00 – Every advisor experiences it: hand in the vent, water on treated glass, odor check
- 12:00 – Advisors capture before/after photo or video on their phones
- 15:00 – Around the room: one-sentence customer share from each advisor
- 20:00 – Set the rule: nobody offers it until they've experienced it

**Your move**
Next product launch, call your rep and schedule the demo first. Nobody offers it until they've experienced it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/15 plus mins/Menu Offerings 3 — Savings Trivia Contest
title: Menu Offerings 3 — Savings Trivia Contest
best_used_for: Your advisor presents the menu, the customer asks what they're saving — and the advisor reaches for a calculator.
body_md:
**Set**
Menu (3 of 4)

**Bring**
A savings sheet you've figured for every menu bundle (bundle price vs. à la carte), and a 'trivia champ' trinket for the winner's desk.

**Word tracks**
- “Menu trivia. I name the bundle, you name the savings. First one right gets the point. Winner takes home the trivia champ trophy.”
- “When you present the menu today, lead with what they save. Customers buy the savings.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why savings sell: customers get excited about what they SAVE
- 3:00 – Walk the team through each bundle's savings; they take notes
- 10:00 – Trivia rounds: name the bundle, they name the savings
- 20:00 – Crown the trivia champ; trinket goes on their desk
- 22:00 – Standard: lead every menu presentation today with the savings

**Your move**
Put the trinket on the winner's desk where the whole drive can see it — and announce the rematch date.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/15 plus mins/Role Play Brake Pitches — Go Around the Room
title: Role Play Brake Pitches — Go Around the Room
workbook_title: Role Play Brake Pitches — Go Around the Room
situation_tags: Attach rate or ticket flat|New hire or onboarding|Objections and deferred work
best_used_for: Weekly team meeting. New advisors on the drive. Or a brake attach rate that's gone soft.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE sample vehicle sheet for everyone (year, make, mileage, brake measurements, recommended services), a stopwatch, and the eight-point checklist.

**Word tracks**
- “Everybody's pitching the same car. Forty-five seconds minimum. I'm timing you, and I'm listening for eight things.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Hand out the vehicle sheet and eight-point checklist
- 3:00 – Rotation begins: 45-second minimum pitches, stopwatch running
- 5:00 – After each pitch: one 'liked', one 'change' from teammates (~2 min per advisor)
- 20:00 – Run it back: weakest pitch goes again
- 25:00 – Close: checklist goes on the drive

**Your move**
Build the vehicle sheet tonight. Run the rotation at your next team meeting. Then keep the checklist on your desk and listen for the eight on the drive. *Academy: SMA 120 Language and Process Standards (weeks 9–12); revisited in SMA 220*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/15 plus mins/Set the Interval Chart Standard — Every Advisor, Every Visit
title: Set the Interval Chart Standard — Every Advisor, Every Visit
workbook_title: Set the Interval Chart Standard — Every Advisor, Every Visit
situation_tags: Attach rate or ticket flat|Standards and process
best_used_for: Your fluid exchange offers are inconsistent. One advisor offers everything. The next offers nothing. Same customers. Same vehicles.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your manufacturer's maintenance schedules, your current service menu, and a blank interval chart; plan on 20–30 minutes.

**Word tracks**
- “If you're looking at a fluid to decide whether to offer a service, you're doing it wrong. The interval is the decision-maker. The fluid's appearance is irrelevant to whether you offer it.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Open: 'I didn't think they needed it' — why the chart exists
- 3:00 – Pick intervals as a team, service by service, per manufacturer interval and store standard
- 15:00 – Write the chart; one copy at every desk
- 18:00 – Drill: call a mileage, team calls the services; then reverse
- 25:00 – Set the inspection: five ROs per advisor every Friday; deferred items logged on the RO

**Your move**
Build the chart with your team. Post it at every desk. Pull five ROs per advisor on Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/15 plus mins/WOW Factor Meeting
title: WOW Factor Meeting
best_used_for: The week you launch a product, a contest, or a focus item.
body_md:
**Bring**
The product itself, your parts manager (inventory and tools confirmed the day before), and the certified technician who performs the service with a before-and-after photo or video.

**Word tracks**
- “Before you leave this room, I want to hear your WOW in one sentence — the thing you'll share that makes a customer say, 'I didn't know that.'”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why this matters: the advisor who knows something the customer doesn't
- 2:00 – Parts manager: product in hands, label, what's in the box
- 6:00 – Certified technician: before-and-after photo or video of the condition it corrects
- 10:00 – Each advisor shares their ONE 'WOW' fact in one sentence
- 14:00 – ONE advisor teaches it back to the room as the expert
- 16:00 – End

**Your move**
Pick the product. Check the shelf. Get parts and your certified technician in the room — and make your advisors the experts.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/Have a Team Meeting Before Selling New Services
title: Have a Team Meeting Before Selling New Services
workbook_title: Have a Team Meeting Before Selling New Services
best_used_for: The week before any new service goes live on your menu.
body_md:
**Bring**
The new service, a photo or video of the condition it addresses, and the time it takes in the bay.

**Word tracks**
- “There is someone's daughter or grandson riding in that vehicle. You want to be the person who said four minutes wasn't worth it?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Introduce the new service: what condition it addresses, bay time
- 2:00 – Both sides voice the hard part (techs and advisors)
- 5:00 – The appeal: someone's daughter or grandson in that vehicle
- 7:00 – Commitment: techs grade it every vehicle; advisors offer it every time it shows
- 10:00 – Launch date set

**Your move**
Before the next new service launches, get both teams in the room. Ten minutes. Willingness first.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/Long-Interval Vehicles — Honesty Works
title: Long-Interval Vehicles — Honesty Works
situation_tags: Product knowledge and launches|Language and word tracks
best_used_for: Any time your team services long-interval vehicles and the 5,000-mile service conversation gets clumsy.
body_md:
**Bring**
A sample maintenance schedule from a long-interval manufacturer program you service.

**Word tracks**
- “We don't say the manufacturer recommends it. We say this is what we find is in our customers' best interest.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The policy gap advisors feel on long-interval vehicles
- 2:00 – Share the ONE sentence
- 4:00 – Why it works: honest, compliance-safe, respects the manufacturer
- 6:00 – Role play: customer says 'the manual says longer'
- 11:00 – Standard: every advisor on long-interval programs uses this framing

**Your move**
listen to ONE long-interval write-up from every advisor. If you don't hear the sentence, coach it on the spot.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/Main Shop Blinders — Primary Concern First, But Don't Ignore the Rest
title: Main Shop Blinders — Primary Concern First, But Don't Ignore the Rest
workbook_title: Main Shop Blinders — Primary Concern First, But Don't Ignore the Rest
situation_tags: Attach rate or ticket flat|Technicians and the shop
best_used_for: Your main-shop ROs are either getting blown up — or coming back with one line on them.
body_md:
**Bring**
Five recent main-shop ROs with MPIs (one blown-up, one single-line if you have them) and a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “Just because I have a busted heater core doesn't mean I might not need wipers or a license plate bulb. We have to pay attention to detail.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Share the story: both mistakes
- 2:00 – Mitch's line: no blinders
- 3:00 – Teach the two-step: primary first, blinders off after
- 5:00 – Pair role play, switch roles
- 9:00 – Set the standard: five main-shop ROs inspected weekly

**Your move**
Run it Tuesday. Pull your five ROs Friday. Celebrate the advisor who got the big yes AND the wipers.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/Menu Offerings 1 — Your Favorite Part of the Menu
