title: Menu Offerings 1 — Your Favorite Part of the Menu
workbook_title: Menu Offerings 1 — Your Favorite Part of the Menu
best_used_for: Menu sales are flat. Your advisors are presenting the menu like they're reading a takeout order.
body_md:
**Set**
Menu (1 of 4)

**Bring**
A printed copy of your menu for every advisor and a whiteboard for the story board.

**Word tracks**
- “___ picked the cabin filter. Who's got a story about why that matters to a customer?”
- “Today, every menu you present gets ONE story. Your favorite. Share it like you mean it — because you do.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Menu sales are driven by consistency — and belief
- 1:00 – Around the room: every advisor names their favorite part of the menu
- 4:00 – Cross-talk: advisors share what they like about each other's picks
- 7:00 – Build the story board: one story per menu item
- 10:00 – Send them out: ONE story on every menu presentation today

**Your move**
Keep the story board up all week. Every time an advisor sells a menu with a story, they add their initials next to it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/Menu Offerings 2 — Safety and Savings
title: Menu Offerings 2 — Safety and Savings
best_used_for: Menu sales are soft, or an advisor is presenting the menu as a price list.
body_md:
**Set**
Menu (2 of 4)

**Bring**
Your menu and a whiteboard with two columns: Safety and Savings.

**Word tracks**
- “These items are bundled for your safety and savings.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Give the line: 'bundled for your safety and savings'
- 2:00 – Item by item: each advisor puts a menu item in Safety or Savings
- 6:00 – Flip it: find the other column for each item
- 9:00 – Role play: full menu in under a minute, every item framed
- 12:00 – Set the week's listening standard

**Your move**
Listen to ONE menu presentation per advisor. Every item should land in a column. Coach the ones that don't — same day.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/Menu Offerings 4 — Personal Testimony
title: Menu Offerings 4 — Personal Testimony
best_used_for: You've got ONE or two advisors whose menu numbers trail the team.
body_md:
**Set**
Menu (4 of 4)

**Bring**
Your menu and the current list of discounts and vendor offers.

**Word tracks**
- “Pick any item on our menu that you've had done on your own vehicle. Share it with me like I'm your customer.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Preselling vs. selling after the MPI
- 2:00 – Ask for the personal story about a menu item on their own vehicle
- 5:00 – Tighten it to 30 seconds; run it twice
- 9:00 – Load the current discounts and vendor offers
- 12:00 – Set the five-day story standard and the end-of-week check

**Your move**
Every underperforming advisor shares their personal story on every menu presentation for five days. Sit down with each one at the end of the week and look at the menu numbers together.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/Mini-Meeting — Old Products
title: Mini-Meeting — Old Products
situation_tags: Start of month|Product knowledge and launches
best_used_for: Early in the month, once the big meetings are done.
body_md:
**Bring**
Attach rate by advisor on alignments, balances, filters, batteries and bulbs (sales divided by opportunities), a stack of that advisor's ROs for a battery-test spot check, and a sample of any newer product you stock.

**Word tracks**
- “We are not GUESSING that you need an alignment. This machine is precise, and this service will protect your tire investment.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Show the advisor their attach rate on the five items; monetize the gap
- 2:00 – ONE fix for their weakest item (alignment line, '...and balance?', show-and-sell filters, battery test, walk-around bulbs)
- 5:00 – One-stop shop: body shop, main line, detail
- 7:00 – Pick ONE newer product to offer this week
- 8:00 – Set the target and the date you'll check it

**Inspect it**
Batteries and bulbs. Are we testing batteries? Spot check a stack of ROs. Bulbs — back to the walk-around, with the customer participating.

**Your move**
Pull attach rate on these five, find each advisor's ONE weak spot, and give them five minutes and ONE fix.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/Pick Your Low-Hanging Fruit First — Then Stack
title: Pick Your Low-Hanging Fruit First — Then Stack
workbook_title: Pick Your Low-Hanging Fruit First — Then Stack
situation_tags: Product knowledge and launches|Attach rate or ticket flat
best_used_for: You're adding services to a quick lane — or any drive — and the team is reluctant.
body_md:
**Bring**
Attach rate report for the first service you're launching (by advisor), plus a short list of the services you plan to stack after it.

**Word tracks**
- “We're adding ONE service this month. Not five. ONE. Everybody offers it, every time, until it's a habit.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why five-at-once fails
- 2:00 – The three tests; name the ONE service
- 4:00 – Certified technician walks through their part and the photo or video MPI
- 6:00 – Drill the offer around the room
- 8:00 – Define 'normalized' and show the stack order

**Your move**
Name your ONE. Launch it Monday. Inspect the attach rate report every Friday — and don't add number two until the first one is automatic.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/5-15 mins/The 110K Transmission Rule
title: The 110K Transmission Rule
situation_tags: New hire or onboarding|Product knowledge and launches
best_used_for: Every new advisor's first week. Then again every quarter.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your write-up checklist, with a new line added: mileage, then history, then recommendation.

**Word tracks**
- “Over 110K with no history is not an exchange. It's a full transmission evaluation referral. Every time.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why this rule is non-negotiable
- 2:00 – The varnish story: what happens over 110K with no history
- 5:00 – Walk the checklist: mileage, history, recommendation
- 8:00 – Quick drill: call out three vehicles, advisors give the right path
- 11:00 – Lock it on the checklist; inspect write-ups this week

**Your move**
pull every transmission recommendation on vehicles over 110K. Check that the history was verified first.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/Under 5 mins/Send Product Sheets With Estimates
title: Send Product Sheets With Estimates
situation_tags: Attach rate or ticket flat|Objections and deferred work
best_used_for: Your fluid exchange attach rate is soft. Or customers keep asking "is this really necessary?" on estimates.
body_md:
**Bring**
The product performance sheet for each recommended fluid service, and a sample estimate in your texting platform.

**Word tracks**
- “I've attached the product sheet so you can see exactly what goes into your vehicle. Take a look, and I'm right here if you have questions.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Teach it: every fluid estimate goes out with the product sheet (transparency + credibility)
- 1:00 – Model it: attach the link to a live estimate on screen
- 2:00 – Drill it: each advisor builds ONE estimate with the link, plus the advisor line
- 4:00 – Set the standard and the Friday spot check (five estimates per advisor)

**Inspect it**
Spot-check five estimates per advisor this week. Link attached or not. Simple.

**Your move**
Load the product sheets into your texting platform today. Spot-check on Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/Under 5 mins/Use AI to Fill Product Knowledge Gaps
title: Use AI to Fill Product Knowledge Gaps
workbook_title: Use AI to Fill Product Knowledge Gaps
best_used_for: An advisor gets stuck on a product question. Somebody says, "We'll cover that in the next class."
body_md:
**Bring**
One real product question from yesterday's drive and an advisor's phone.

**Word tracks**
- “Open any AI tool. Type it in right now: shocks and struts on this truck, benefits and how to share it with a customer.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Pick ONE real product question from yesterday's drive
- 0:30 – An advisor types it into any AI tool, live
- 1:00 – Advisor shares the answer back in their own words
- 2:30 – Guardrail: AI for knowledge, technician grading for this vehicle

**Your move**
Every morning, pick ONE product question your team fumbled yesterday. One advisor looks it up live. One advisor shares it back.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Menu, Attach Rate and Launches/Under 5 mins/…And? …With? — The Piggyback Sale
title: …And? …With? — The Piggyback Sale
best_used_for: Ticket averages are flat. Advisors are writing the one thing the customer came in for — and stopping.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your five chosen piggyback sales written on the board.

**Word tracks**
- “Upsells are basic. Not easy — just basic. One more word on every RO. And. Or with.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The two words: 'and' and 'with'
- 1:00 – Reveal the five piggybacks for the week
- 2:00 – Rapid-fire drill: manager calls the service, advisors fire back the piggyback
- 4:00 – Standard: ONE piggyback offered on every RO today

**Your move**
Pull five ROs from each advisor at the end of the day. Look for the "and" or the "with." Recognize the advisor with the most at tomorrow's huddle.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/15 plus mins/Numbers Meeting
title: Numbers Meeting
best_used_for: Day 2 of the month. Right after your Fast Start.
body_md:
**Bring**
Reports by advisor with your written ANALYSIS, ONE specific opportunity per advisor, a skipped-area training plan with reward and 'scarlet letter', a day-of-week sales tracker, and your marketing calendar and any new-product launch details.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Open: no Q&A today — this is a Vision Meeting
- 2:00 – Numbers inside the numbers: ONE specific item per advisor (praise specific)
- 10:00 – Team trends: skipped area, training announcement, reward and 'scarlet letter' (criticize general)
- 14:00 – Profit success story and day-of-week sales pattern
- 17:00 – Set the vision: seasonal focus, upcoming marketing, new product; hand out tools

**Your move**
Run your reports, write ONE specific item for each advisor, and walk in with a vision — not a question. *Academy: SMA 201 Weekly Meetings (weeks 13–16); revisited in SMA 401*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/15 plus mins/The Coaching Audit — A Meeting With Yourself
title: The Coaching Audit — A Meeting With Yourself
workbook_title: The Coaching Audit — A Meeting With Yourself
best_used_for: Mid-month. Day ten to fifteen. Close the door. Phone face down.
body_md:
**Set**
Find the Few

**Bring**
A blank sheet, your calendar, and your attach rate report with RO counts by advisor.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – List every advisor's name
- 3:00 – Count prepared coaching conversations (sit-down, data, specific ask) per advisor this month
- 7:00 – Lay the attach rate report beside the list; find the highest-RO, lowest-attach-rate advisor
- 11:00 – Ask: is my coaching energy where it moves the most revenue?
- 14:00 – Book the rest of the month's prepared conversations: name, date, ONE ask

**Your move**
Run the audit. Then book your first prepared conversation with your highest-RO, lowest-attach-rate advisor — before you open your email.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/5-15 mins/Days of the Week
title: Days of the Week
best_used_for: The month is grinding. The big numbers aren't moving. Your team needs a win they can get today.
body_md:
**Bring**
Production by day of the week for your five most influential op codes (or a blank record board if you're starting today), and a lunch budget.

**Word tracks**
- “The record for this on a Wednesday is ___. Break it today and lunch is on me.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Not every day is created equal: why DAY-ly records matter
- 2:00 – Reveal the day-of-week records for five op codes on the board
- 5:00 – Launch the challenge: break a record, lunch is on you
- 8:00 – Each advisor names the record they're chasing today
- 10:00 – Close: records announced and celebrated at the next huddle

**Your move**
Pick your five services. Write today's day-of-the-week records on the board before the doors open — and be ready to buy the first lunch.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/5-15 mins/Fast Start Meeting
title: Fast Start Meeting
best_used_for: The first business day of the month. Every month.
body_md:
**Bring**
Leftover-business report from last month by advisor, last month's results, a written contest sheet (payout, bogey, length, qualifiers, escalator), and an inventory check on any featured product.

**Word tracks**
- “We're all here to make money. We'll do it by offering everything a customer needs and nothing they don't — and making every customer count.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives from last month and ONE item that needs greater focus
- 2:00 – Close out last month: leftover business, open ROs, accountability
- 4:00 – Launch the Fast Start Contest: payout, bogey, length
- 8:00 – Qualifiers and the whole-team escalator
- 10:00 – Inventory check on featured items; close on core values and the 'every customer counts' line

**Your move**
Here's your move this month. Set your payout, your bogey and your length before Day 1 — and announce it in the first five minutes.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/5-15 mins/Find Your ONE — The Advisor With the Most Opportunity
title: Find Your ONE — The Advisor With the Most Opportunity
workbook_title: Find Your ONE — The Advisor With the Most Opportunity
best_used_for: Day two or three of the month. Last month is closed. The report is fresh.
body_md:
**Set**
Find the Few

**Bring**
Last month's attach rate report, ranked by advisor, with RO counts.

**Word tracks**
- “A few of us are producing most of our results. And I can prove it on our report right now.”
- “I am not asking you to change what everyone is doing. I am asking you to find the one thing our top advisors are doing differently — and teach it to the rest of us.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Put the ranked report on the table: 'I can prove it on our report right now'
- 1:00 – Walk the ranking top to bottom; let the report do the talking
- 5:00 – Privately note the advisor with the highest RO count and lowest attach rate (your one-on- one this week)
- 7:00 – Close with the ask: find the one thing the top advisors do differently and teach it to the rest
- 10:00 – End; schedule the one-on-one before Friday

**Your move**
Pull the report. Rank it. Circle ONE name — high RO count, low attach rate. Get that conversation on the calendar before Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/5-15 mins/Goals One-on-One
title: Goals One-on-One
best_used_for: About Day 6. Seven or eight minutes per advisor.
body_md:
**Bring**
Each advisor's goal sheet and month-to-date pace, Fast Start contest standings, ONE positive and ONE monetized opportunity written for each advisor, and the department's pace.

**Word tracks**
- “Were you tracking your own numbers, or waiting for me to do it for you?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Advisor pace: exceeding, meeting, or behind — and the matching move
- 2:00 – Contest standings; tracking their own numbers (Measurable, Trackable, Attainable)
- 4:00 – A positive from the goal sheet
- 5:00 – ONE monetized area of opportunity
- 7:00 – Department pace: what's working, ONE team gap

**Your move**
Write ONE positive and ONE opportunity for every advisor before you sit down — then give each of them their eight minutes.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/5-15 mins/Mid-Month Numbers — Tracking Goals
title: Mid-Month Numbers — Tracking Goals
best_used_for: Mid-month. One-on-one. Ten to fifteen minutes per advisor.
body_md:
**Bring**
Each advisor's pace report: % of gross goal now vs. needed, last month's halfway mark and finish, Effective Labor Rate, the top 8–10 gross drivers, walk-around items (tires, batteries, nitrogen, wipers), lot damage numbers, and MPI items with closing %.

**Word tracks**
- “Let's take your annual goal and turn it into quarterly, monthly, daily, and per RO. Now, for each item: what's your plan, your pitch, the feature, the benefit, the common objection, and how you'll handle it?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Pace: % of gross goal now vs. needed; open ROs; last month's halfway vs. finish
- 3:00 – Effective Labor Rate: findings from your prep
- 5:00 – Walk-around items together; cross-check lot damage
- 8:00 – MPI items: pace and closing % on filters, brakes, belts, fluid exchanges
- 11:00 – Goal breakdown: annual → quarterly → monthly → daily → per RO; plan, pitch, feature, benefit, objection
- 14:00 – Close: together, we work better

**Your move**
Pull the top 8 to 10 gross drivers for every advisor. Book fifteen minutes with each one before the month hits the halfway mark.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/5-15 mins/Where the Money Lives — Your Top SKUs
title: Where the Money Lives — Your Top SKUs
workbook_title: Where the Money Lives — Your Top SKUs
situation_tags: Start of month|Attach rate or ticket flat
best_used_for: Week two. Enough volume on the board to see a pattern.
body_md:
**Set**
Find the Few

**Bring**
Revenue-by-SKU report (with units by advisor for your top SKUs).

**Word tracks**
- “These are the items that pay all of us. Let's look at who's carrying them.”
- “Your top three SKUs. One feature and one benefit for each. Go.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Show the top 3–4 SKUs carrying the majority of gross
- 3:00 – Ownership question: is ONE advisor carrying all the volume?
- 5:00 – Rapid-fire drill: one feature + one benefit for the top three SKUs, 30 seconds each
- 10:00 – Flag the zeros; schedule private training-vs-process diagnosis
- 12:00 – End

**Your move**
Pull the SKU report. Find your top three. Run the drill. Then sit down with every zero and diagnose before you prescribe.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/5-15 mins/Where the Yes Is Decided — The First Minutes of the Visit
title: Where the Yes Is Decided — The First Minutes of the Visit
workbook_title: Where the Yes Is Decided — The First Minutes of the Visit
situation_tags: Start of month|Phones and BDC|Attach rate or ticket flat
best_used_for: Week one or two, when your MPI conversion or your phone sale rate is soft.
body_md:
**Set**
Find the Few

**Bring**
Blank paper, pens, and your MPI conversion report.

**Word tracks**
- “Write your send-off speech, word for word, the way you said it to your last customer. You've got three minutes.”
- “Seven for seven. Every customer, every time. I'll be on the drive listening this week.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the first few minutes: walk-around, write-up, send-off speech
- 2:00 – Advisors write their send-off speech from memory (3 minutes)
- 5:00 – Reveal the seven elements
- 8:00 – Advisors self-grade; collect papers as your coaching agenda
- 11:00 – Set the seven-for-seven standard and the drive inspection

**Your move**
Run the drill. Keep the papers. Then stand on the drive, listen for all seven, and coach the ONE that's missing.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/Under 5 mins/Celebrate Milestones — Not Just the Final Goal
title: Celebrate Milestones — Not Just the Final Goal
workbook_title: Celebrate Milestones — Not Just the Final Goal
best_used_for: It's the first huddle of the month. Or the big number isn't moving and your team's starting to feel it.
body_md:
**Bring**
The goal board with this month's milestone per advisor, and a small recognition token.

**Word tracks**
- “___ crossed into Strong this month on transmission fluid services. That's not the finish line. That's a mile marker — and mile markers get celebrated here.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why a December-only goal dies in March
- 1:00 – Post this month's milestone next to each advisor's name
- 2:00 – Recognize anyone who crossed a milestone (e.g., Low to Strong)
- 3:30 – Name the next team milestone on the board

**Your move**
Here's your move this month. Put ONE milestone per advisor on the board this week. The first one who crosses it gets recognized at the next huddle — in front of everybody.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Monthly Rhythm and Numbers/Under 5 mins/Orange Chicken
title: Orange Chicken
best_used_for: End of the month. The team's dragging. Numbers are low and the attitude is lower.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing but your own energy.

**Word tracks**
- “Is your heart pumping right now? Do you feel alive? Did you feel like this with a single customer today?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Yell 'ORANGE CHICKEN!' with no warning
- 0:15 – The three questions while hearts are pounding
- 0:40 – 'Take that feeling to your next customer'
- 0:50 – Send them to the drive

**Your move**
Pick your Orange Chicken. Your own words, your own yell. Bring it to the last huddle of the month.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/15 plus mins/Compile Objections as a Team — Build the Playbook
title: Compile Objections as a Team — Build the Playbook
workbook_title: Compile Objections as a Team — Build the Playbook
best_used_for: Start of a quarter. Ideal when your team is hearing "no" and nobody can say exactly why.
body_md:
**Bring**
A notebook or shared log for each experienced advisor; later, the compiled objection list.

**Word tracks**
- “For the next thirty days, write down every specific reason a customer gives for saying no to any recommendation. Not 'money.' The actual words they used.”

**Run sheet**
- Week 0 (5 min) – Assign the 30-day objection log to experienced advisors
- Day 30, 0:00 – Compile meeting: everyone reads their list aloud
- Day 30, 15:00 – Group duplicates; rank by frequency
- Weekly (15 min) – One objection, one response; use it on the drive
- Following week – Report back; keep what works in the playbook
- End of quarter – Publish the custom objection playbook

**Your move**
Hand out the notebooks. Start the thirty-day clock. Put the compile meeting on the calendar today.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/15 plus mins/Teach Your Advisors to Find One More Move
title: Teach Your Advisors to Find One More Move
workbook_title: Teach Your Advisors to Find One More Move
best_used_for: Your advisors are accepting a flat no as the end of the conversation.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard with three columns: money, time, decision-maker.

**Word tracks**
- “When a customer says no to the full package — what's your one more move?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Share the Checkmate story
- 2:00 – Ask: what's your one more move?
- 4:00 – Three columns: money, time, decision-maker — every advisor gives specific words
- 12:00 – Pair drill: customer throws an objection, advisor makes the move; switch
- 18:00 – Standard: ONE more move on every no; deferred, not declined

**Your move**
Run it at your next team meeting. Type up the best answers from the board and hand them out the next morning. Then listen on the drive for the one more move. *Academy: SMA 210 Op Code Mastery (weeks 17–20); revisited in SMA 201*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/5-15 mins/Close, Close, Close — The Four-Step Close
title: Close, Close, Close — The Four-Step Close
workbook_title: Close, Close, Close — The Four-Step Close
situation_tags: New hire or onboarding|Objections and deferred work|Language and word tracks
best_used_for: Your advisors present well and still don't get the yes. Or any new advisor's first month.
body_md:
**Bring**
A dry erase board with the four steps written before the team walks in.

**Word tracks**
- “You need a set of tires. Your total investment is right here. We can have those on by 3:00. All I need is your authorization.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The four steps on the board: what, how much, when, authorization
- 2:00 – Teach each piece: bundle, 'total investment', target time, statement close
- 6:00 – Drill: strongest advisor closes a brake job; newer advisor closes wipers; tough critique
- 10:00 – Manager models the close rapid-fire around the room
- 12:00 – Set the standard: three presentations inspected daily

**Your move**
Listen to three presentations a day. Inspect the four pieces. Coach the missing one on the spot.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/5-15 mins/Kill the Ignore-Ignore-Acknowledge Three-Strike Approach
title: Kill the Ignore-Ignore-Acknowledge Three-Strike Approach
situation_tags: Objections and deferred work|CSI and surveys
best_used_for: Your veterans are working hard and their survey scores are sliding anyway.
body_md:
**Bring**
Recent survey comments that mention pressure (names removed), and a whiteboard to write the two-attempt standard.

**Word tracks**
- “A lot of us learned ignore, ignore, acknowledge. That was the standard. It isn't anymore. Our standard is two sincere attempts. After the second no, we acknowledge it and protect the relationship.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives about the team's effort
- 1:00 – Name the old three-strike playbook
- 3:00 – Share the new standard: two sincere attempts, then acknowledge
- 6:00 – Role play: second no, acknowledge, preserve the relationship
- 11:00 – Lock the standard and how you'll listen for it

**Your move**
sit in on ONE write-up with each veteran. Listen for the third push — and coach it the moment you hear it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/5-15 mins/Overcoming Objections Meeting
title: Overcoming Objections Meeting
best_used_for: Any week you hear an advisor stall at the counter.
body_md:
**Bring**
A card with the five objections and their redirect phrases for each advisor; nothing else.

**Word tracks**
- “Point at ONE advisor.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Frame it: five objections, five phrases, no hesitation
- 1:00 – Money and budget vs. cash flow; Time and urgency
- 4:00 – Understanding, Decision maker, Owner's manual (embrace vs. deflect)
- 8:00 – Rapid-fire around the room, multiple laps
- 12:00 – Seek the NO: assign the decline log for this week

**Your move**
Run the rapid-fire every morning until nobody hesitates.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/5-15 mins/Redirects
title: Redirects
situation_tags: Objections and deferred work|Underperformance or accountability
best_used_for: You've got advisors who hear "not today" and just — stop. Deferred, not declined — but they never even try to turn it around.
body_md:
**Bring**
A stack of recent ROs with deferred items, and a pocket card with the seven redirects.

**Word tracks**
- “An objection isn't a no. It's a request for more information. Pick a redirect and share why it matters.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Every objection is a fork in the road
- 2:00 – Hand out the seven redirects
- 4:00 – Manager models a redirect on a real deferred item
- 7:00 – Paired drill: customer objects, advisor redirects; swap
- 12:00 – Standard: ONE redirect attempt before any item is deferred

**Your move**
Pull ONE deferred item per underperforming advisor each day. Have them show you which redirect they used. If they didn't use one, run it together on the spot.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/5-15 mins/Seek the No
title: Seek the No
best_used_for: Any week. Announce it a week ahead — because the homework is the meeting.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard; advisors bring the objections they jotted down during the week.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Each advisor reads their best objection, customer's exact words
- 4:00 – Sort them into buckets (price, time, trust, next time)
- 7:00 – Solve the biggest bucket as a team: who turned this into a yes?
- 11:00 – Lock in the winning response; everybody says it once
- 13:00 – End; reassign the homework

**Your move**
Assign the homework today. Run the meeting next week. Then seek the no all over again — because every no you study is one you'll never lose the same way twice.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/5-15 mins/The Space Between Stimulus and Response Is Where Thinking Lives
title: The Space Between Stimulus and Response Is Where Thinking Lives
workbook_title: The Space Between Stimulus and Response Is Where Thinking Lives
best_used_for: Your team is folding at the first no. "Okay, no problem" before the customer even finishes the sentence.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard and marker.

**Word tracks**
- “Advisors who respond instead of react close more over time. Not because they talk more. Because they think in the space.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Frankl's line; draw stimulus / space / response
- 2:00 – Collapsed space vs. wide space
- 4:00 – The three questions on the board
- 6:00 – Drill: manager says no, advisor pauses and responds
- 10:00 – Bloom's six levels; standard: classify every deferred no

**Your move**
For every deferred item on a closed RO, ask the advisor ONE thing: which no was it? First or second. Price or value. Never or not today.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/Under 5 mins/Advocates to Our Customers — The Partnership Word
title: Advocates to Our Customers — The Partnership Word
workbook_title: Advocates to Our Customers — The Partnership Word
best_used_for: Your team is polite, professional — and passive. Waiting to be asked. Deferred work sitting on the books for months.
body_md:
**Bring**
Yesterday's deferred-items list.

**Word tracks**
- “We want to be advocates to our customers. We want to say, you're not alone in this decision. I can help you make this decision. I can help you make the proper decision.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Ask for the one-sentence job description
- 1:00 – Helper vs. advocate on the board
- 2:00 – Share Mitch's advocate words
- 3:00 – Drill: each advisor shares ONE deferred item as the advocate
- 4:30 – Standard: rewrite the job description with 'advocate'; deferred call-backs

**Your move**
Pull ONE deferred item per advisor and have them call it back — as the advocate.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/Under 5 mins/Send Financing Preemptively — Before the Call, Not After the No
title: Send Financing Preemptively — Before the Call, Not After the No
workbook_title: Send Financing Preemptively — Before the Call, Not After the No
situation_tags: Objections and deferred work|Phones and BDC
best_used_for: Your third-party financing option is sitting there, and your advisors only reach for it after the no.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing. Optional: your financing application report by advisor.

**Word tracks**
- “Starting today, the link goes out before the call. Every time.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The problem: financing only after the no
- 1:00 – The elevation: send the link before the call
- 2:00 – Manager models the line
- 3:00 – Each advisor says it once
- 4:30 – Standard: link goes out first above your dollar threshold

**Your move**
Run the huddle tomorrow. Then check your financing applications Friday and see who's sending first.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Objections and Deferred Work/Under 5 mins/Third-Party Financing — Offer It at Active Delivery Too
title: Third-Party Financing — Offer It at Active Delivery Too
workbook_title: Third-Party Financing — Offer It at Active Delivery Too
best_used_for: Your deferred list keeps growing, and those deferred items aren't coming back in.
body_md:
**Bring**
Five ROs from yesterday with deferred items; your third-party financing program's current terms.

**Word tracks**
- “Financing isn't just an objection handler. It's how we set up next visit's yes before the customer leaves the parking lot.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Reframe: financing sets up next visit's yes
- 1:00 – Model the delivery line; deferred, not declined
- 2:00 – Drill on yesterday's real deferred-item ROs
- 3:30 – Confirm program terms
- 4:30 – Standard: every deferred item gets the mention

**Your move**
Friday, pull ten deferred-item ROs and ask each advisor what they shared at delivery. Then track how many of those customers come back for the deferred work.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/A/C Evaporator Cleaning Boost Meeting
title: A/C Evaporator Cleaning Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your A/C evaporator cleaning attach rate trails your cabin air filter sales. And every spring.
body_md:
**Bring**
A dirty cabin air filter and a new one; a photo or video MPI clip showing where the evaporator sits.

**Word tracks**
- “Your cabin filter has been catching debris. Here's the video. No filter is perfect, so my certified technician Hector recommends cleaning the evaporator right behind it while the filter's out.”
- “We can do that. The filter catches what's coming in. The evaporator cleaning takes care of what already got past it.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: A/C evaporator cleaning attach rate by advisor (on screen); dirty filter prop
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: no filter is perfect; musty odor, weak airflow
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: dirty vs new filter on the photo or video MPI; show where the evaporator sits; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line, three-part cabin air filter bundle pairing (cabin filter, A/C performance treatment); bundle coverage per your chemical company, "just the filter" objection
- 8:00 – The challenge: evaporator cleaning on every cabin filter recommendation (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. Every cabin filter recommendation carries the evaporator cleaning with it this week. No standalone filter recommendations. Track it daily. Friday, you inspect the match.

**Your move**
Friday, recognize the advisor with the tightest match between cabin filters and evaporator cleanings.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/A/C Recharge Boost Meeting
title: A/C Recharge Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your A/C recharge attach rate falls below your best month. And every spring, before the first hot week.
body_md:
**Bring**
A dirty cabin air filter; a photo or video MPI clip showing a vent temperature reading; a whiteboard for the spot-check tally.

**Word tracks**
- “Hot weather is coming. How is your air conditioning working?”
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends an A/C recharge. Here's the vent temperature he graded.”
- “Topping it off doesn't fix a leak. We diagnose first, so you're not back here next month.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: A/C recharge attach rate by advisor (on screen); each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: weak airflow, warm vents, musty odor; vehicle's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: vent temperature on the photo or video MPI; right tools for the refrigerant types you see; identify before quoting
- 6:00 – The word track drill: seasonal opening question, Hector line, cabin filter and A/C performance treatment pairings, "just top it off" objection
- 8:00 – The challenge: A/C question on every write-up; spot-check five ROs a day (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. The A/C question gets asked on every write-up this week. You spot-check five ROs a day. Was the question asked? Did the cabin filter ride along? Friday, you post the results.

**Your move**
Recognize the advisor who asked it on every single ticket. Then keep the question on the write-up all season.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/A/C System Check Boost Meeting
title: A/C System Check Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Every spring, before the first hot week. And any week your A/C system check attach rate falls below your best month.
body_md:
**Bring**
The A/C testing equipment rolled into the room for a live demo; a photo or video MPI clip of A/C readings.

**Word tracks**
- “Before the hot days get here, let's make sure your air conditioning is ready. We'd like to check it for you.”
- “My certified technician Hector graded your A/C system. Here's the video of the readings.”
- “Great. Then the check confirms it before the first hot day.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: A/C system check attach rate by advisor (on screen); each advisor does the math on the next yes

Last — the challenge. Every advisor offers the A/C system check on every RO this week. And by Friday, every advisor and every tech has run the equipment once in front of you. You inspect it Friday.

**Your move**
A short huddle with the equipment pays off on every hot day of the season. Make it the standard.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/AC Performance

- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: before-and-after vent temperature on the photo or video MPI
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line, A/C recharge pairing, "my A/C works fine" objection, active delivery resell at the staged vehicle; dealership's voice
- 8:00 – The challenge: treatment offered on every recharge, active delivery on every treatment (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. Every A/C recharge gets the treatment offered this week, and every treatment gets an active delivery. Match recharges against treatments daily. Friday, you inspect the match.

**Your move**
Friday, recognize the advisor with the tightest match, and the best delivery you saw.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Alternator Test Boost Meeting

- 8:00 – The challenge: both tests together every time; you check five video MPIs Friday

Friday, you pull five video MPIs with a battery test and check that the alternator test is on every one.

**Your move**
Announce the standard at this meeting. Inspect Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Battery Replacement Boost Meeting
title: Battery Replacement Boost Meeting

ONE strong video MPI clip showing a battery test; A used battery from the bench, if you have one

Post every battery Hector grades in the red on the board, with the advisor's name and the offer. Friday, reds graded and offers made should match.

Pair your struggling advisor with your best certified technician today. Inspect Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Battery Terminal Service Boost Meeting

Friday, you count the before-and-after photo or video pairs. Most pairs wins lunch.

End this meeting in the drive with a hood up.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Battery Test Boost Meeting

Run the video audit before this meeting. Let the count start the conversation.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Brake Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
title: Brake Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting

body_md:

A sample of dark brake fluid next to fresh amber fluid.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends a brake fluid exchange.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: two wins; brake fluid exchange attach rate by advisor from the screen; each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: All Fluids Go Bad, time first; calipers, master cylinder, booster; pedal feel; store coverage only if offered

- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line; "I just added some" response; brake pads pairing; deferred, not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: brake fluid conversation on every brake pad job all week; every brake RO inspected Friday

Wednesday, play the customer. Walk up to each advisor's kiosk with a brake job and see if the brake fluid conversation comes up without a prompt. Friday, you check every brake RO.

Set a dark fluid sample next to fresh amber on the counter Monday and leave it there all week.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Brake Noise Treatment Boost Meeting
title: Brake Noise Treatment Boost Meeting

- “We include a brake noise treatment with your brake service so your new brakes stay quiet and work the way they should.”

- 8:00 – The challenge: brake noise treatment on every brake job all week; every brake RO inspected Friday

Parts tracks it. Friday, you inspect every brake RO for the kit.

Invite your parts manager to Monday's meeting today.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Brake Pads Front Boost Meeting
title: Brake Pads Front Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your front brake pad attach rate falls below your best month, or reds on the MPI are getting deferred without a call back.
body_md:
**Bring**
A box of your front brake pads from parts; a worn pad next to a new one; a small prize; your store's coverage sheet for the pads, if it offers one.

**Word tracks**
- “Your certified technician measured your front pads, and they're yellow. Your pads have done their job. Let's replace them before the noise starts.”
- “By the time they squeak, the metal tab is touching the rotor. Today, it's just pads.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the front brake pad attach rate by advisor; not measuring or not offering
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: The wear indicator scrapes the rotor; by then the customer is late
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector measures the pads and gives the color on every photo or video MPI; percentage of life left describes green, yellow, red; Hector's voice; your measurements and equipment set the numbers
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Parts shares product knowledge; know your parts warranty and share it on every pad recommendation; reward the best fact; around the room; the "wait till they squeak" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: Front pads measured and shared on every MPI; five MPIs a day, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Make it a contest. Every pad measured on video earns a jar ticket. Friday, draw for lunch.

**Your move**
Hang that winning fact on the board, and have every advisor use it ONE time before Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Brake Pads Rear Boost Meeting
title: Brake Pads Rear Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your rear brake pad attach rate trails your front pads. Hector measures both.
body_md:
**Bring**
A box of your rear brake pads from parts; five recent photo or video MPI clips; a small prize; your store's coverage sheet for the pads, if it offers one.

**Word tracks**
- “Your certified technician graded all four corners. Your fronts are green. Your rears are yellow. Let's take care of the rears today, before they start making noise.”

- 6:00 – The word track drill: Parts shares product knowledge; know your parts warranty and share it on every pad recommendation; around the room; tire rotation pairing; the "just had brakes" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: Rear pad measurements on every MPI; five MPIs a day, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Thursday, you and Hector walk five MPIs together. Any rear corner that wasn't measured gets fixed that day. Friday, you check the rear pad attach rate by advisor.

**Your move**
Find ONE certified technician grading all four corners every time, and make them the example in next Monday's huddle.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Breather Filter Boost Meeting

Put the question on the board tonight and run the meeting Monday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Bulb Replacement Boost Meeting

Walk the drive today. Ask three advisors. Let their answers set the tone.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Cabin Air Filter Boost Meeting

Pick your best side-by-side clip and play it Monday morning to set the standard.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Caliper Service Boost Meeting

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Complete Fuel System Service Boost Meeting

A bottle of tank additive; the injector cleaner; a photo or video MPI clip of a drivability grade or borescope view; a whiteboard with the one-, two- and three-part ladder.

Put the ladder on the whiteboard Monday. One-part, two-part, complete. Inspect Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Coolant Exchange Boost Meeting

Put the jar on the service counter Monday and leave it there all week.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Coolant Hoses Boost Meeting

Meet with your certified technicians first. Then start the clock.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Decarb Service Boost Meeting

A photo or video MPI clip of a drivability grade (rough idle or hesitation); a whiteboard.

- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends a decarb service. Here's the video of what he graded.”

Set the standard Monday. Pull the videos Friday. Recognize the advisor who shared it every time.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Differential Filter Boost Meeting

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Differential Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting

Put a sample of dark differential fluid on the service counter Monday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/EV Charge Port Cleaning Boost Meeting

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/EV Rodent Deterrent Boost Meeting

body_md:
**Bring**
A photo or video MPI clip of rodent nesting or chewed wiring, or a clean baseline clip.

**Word tracks**
- “Where do you usually park it?”
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends an EV rodent deterrent. Rodents nest in EVs because there's no warm engine to keep them away.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: EV rodent deterrent attach rate by advisor against EVs written (on screen)
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: no warm engine; high-voltage wiring; damage shows up late
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: nesting, droppings, chewed wiring or a clean baseline on the photo or video MPI; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: parking question, Hector line, flea-protection analogy, EV charge port cleaning pairing
- 8:00 – The challenge: parking question and deterrent offer on every EV write-up (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. "Where do you usually park it" gets asked on every EV write- up this week, and the deterrent gets offered. Friday, you pull every EV RO and inspect it. Was the question asked? Was the deterrent offered?

**Your move**
Recognize the advisor who owned it. The advisor who makes this offer every time wins this service.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Engine Air Filter Boost Meeting
title: Engine Air Filter Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week this attach rate dips, and every spring.
body_md:
**Bring**
A used engine air filter from the shop, a new one, a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “We need to replace your old filter, that has done its job, with a brand new filter made specifically for your model.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: two wins; engine air filter attach rate by advisor from the screen; each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: pass the used filter; protects the engine, MAF sensor and turbo compressor wheel; fuel economy and acceleration; the four voices — the filter is what the vehicle says on the drive and what Hector says after the MPI
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades every filter and shows old next to new on the photo or video MPI; parts manager in the room
- 6:00 – The word track drill: "has done its job" line around the room; cabin air filter pairing; deferred, not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: offer on every walk-around all week; five ROs per advisor pulled and inspected Friday; a reward at forecast and a bigger one well over forecast

**Inspect it**
Wednesday, you ride along on three walk-arounds per advisor and watch for the offer. Friday, you share what you saw, one advisor at a time.

**Your move**
Run it Monday. Inspect Friday. Celebrate whoever moved the needle.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Engine Cleaning Service Boost Meeting
title: Engine Cleaning Service Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week this attach rate dips.
body_md:
**Bring**
A printed engine cleaning checklist for every advisor; a photo or video MPI clip of a dark, gummy dipstick; a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “Think of sludge like cholesterol in the engine. You can't see it from the outside, but it's slowly blocking the passages oil needs.”
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends an engine cleaning service. It's done with your 5,000-mile service, so there's no extra downtime.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: engine cleaning service attach rate by advisor (on screen); each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: sludge and varnish block oil passages; the cholesterol analogy; two products — engine cleaner before the drain, oil additive with the new oil
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades the dipstick and the oil life monitor (single digits) on the photo or video MPI; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: read the checklist, Hector line, 5,000-mile service pairing, "can't swing it" objection (deferred, not declined), locker-room line
- 8:00 – The challenge: checklist live all week; audit ROs against it (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. The checklist is in every advisor's hand tomorrow morning. Every trigger gets the conversation, every time, all week. Friday, you audit the ROs against the checklist.

**Your move**
Run the audit Friday. Recognize the advisor who started the conversation at every trigger point.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Engine Oil Service Boost Meeting
title: Engine Oil Service Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your team is mixing up the oil words, or your engine oil service attach rate falls below your best month.
body_md:
**Bring**
A bottle of the oil additive; a photo or video MPI clip of a graded dipstick; a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends our engine oil service with your 5,000-mile service today. It adds an oil additive that helps protect your engine until your next visit.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: engine oil service attach rate by advisor (on screen) — every 5,000-mile service that left without the oil additive
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: the 5,000-mile service is the oil and filter; the engine oil service adds the oil additive that protects the engine to the next visit; dealership's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades oil condition on the dipstick on the photo or video MPI
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line for the engine oil service; dark, gummy dipstick steps up to the engine cleaning service; deferred, not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: engine oil service offered on every 5,000-mile service all week; ten ROs per advisor inspected Friday

**Inspect it**
Thursday morning, run a two-minute gauntlet. Every advisor delivers the engine oil service offer to you, cold. Friday, you check their 5,000-mile service ROs for the offer, sold or deferred.

**Your move**
Open Monday with "leaders, not order takers," and inspect it Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Front Wiper Blades Boost Meeting
title: Front Wiper Blades Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your front wiper blade attach rate falls below your best month. And right before your rainy or snowy season.
body_md:
**Bring**
A worn front wiper blade from the shop; a whiteboard for the leaderboard.

**Word tracks**
- “Your wipers are streaking across the driver's side. Let's replace them today so you can see clearly in the next storm.”
- “You can. And if we do it today, they're on before you leave, not in a parking lot in the rain.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the front wiper blade attach rate by advisor; do the math with your own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Conditions language; lift the blade at the walk-around with your customer there; vehicle's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades the blades and shows the streak on the photo or video MPI
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Worn blade around the room, windshield treatment pairing, the parts-store response
- 8:00 – The challenge: One-week front wiper blade contest, daily leaderboard, inspect the board Friday and the winner picks lunch

**Inspect it**
Rank your advisors on front wiper blade sales. Front blades only. Post the leaderboard every morning. Friday, you inspect the board, and the winner picks lunch.

**Your move**
Walk the drive twice a day and watch for ONE thing: is the blade getting lifted at the walk-around.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Fuel Filter Boost Meeting
title: Fuel Filter Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week this attach rate dips, especially on diesels and high-mileage trucks.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard for your MPI audit count; a used fuel filter if Hector can pull one.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends replacing your fuel filter.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: two wins; fuel filter attach rate by advisor from the screen; your MPI audit count (75,000 miles and above) on the whiteboard; your five-model in-tank list — opportunity, not criticism
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: protects the fuel pump and injectors; hesitation or rough run under load
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector verifies a serviceable filter, grades it against the manufacturer's schedule, shows it on the photo or video MPI; manufacturer's and Hector's voices
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector recommendation line; engine air filter pairing; "it runs fine" response; deferred, not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: fuel filter check on every vehicle at 75,000 miles and above; re-run the MPI audit Friday and post the change

**Inspect it**
Friday, you run the same audit again. The goal is simple. That count goes down.

**Your move**
Run the audit before Monday. Run it again Friday and post the difference.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Fuel Injector Clean Boost Meeting
title: Fuel Injector Clean Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week this attach rate dips.
body_md:
**Bring**
A bottle of injector cleaner and a bottle of tank additive side by side; a photo or video MPI clip of a drivability grade; a whiteboard for the contest board.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends a fuel injector cleaning. Here's the video of what he graded.”
- “While we're doing your 5,000-mile service, let's add a tank additive to help keep your injectors clean.”
- “You can. Ours goes in with the right service, by a certified technician, and Hector checks the result on the test drive.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: fuel injector clean attach rate by advisor (on screen); each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: deposits break down the spray pattern; rough idle, hesitation, fuel economy; vehicle's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades drivability on the photo or video MPI; share coverage only if your store offers it
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line, tank additive with every fuel injector clean and as the first yes on a 5,000-mile service; throttle body / decarb pairings, parts-store objection; the fuel ladder — tank additive with injector clean is the two-part, add decarb for the complete; walk back any time
- 8:00 – The challenge: week-long fuel injector clean contest board (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. This week is the fuel injector clean contest. ONE board, every advisor. Every fuel injector cleaning that goes on a ticket goes up on the board under that advisor. Friday, you inspect the board and the ROs behind it, and you recognize the leader.

**Your move**
Launch the board Monday. Inspect it Friday. An advisor strong on tank additive but weak on injectors is a coaching opportunity, not just a score.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Headlight Restoration Boost Meeting
title: Headlight Restoration Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your headlight restoration attach rate falls below your best month. And in the fall, when the days get shorter.
body_md:
**Bring**
A before-and-after photo or video MPI clip of a restored headlight from your own shop.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends restoring your headlight lenses. They're cloudy and oxidized. Here's the video.”
- “It does look better. But the bigger reason is how far you can see at night.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: headlight restoration attach rate by advisor (on screen); unoffered, not hidden
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: safety at night, appearance and value; conditions, not opinions; vehicle's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: before-and-after lens photo or video in the MPI
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line and "just cosmetic" objection
- 8:00 – The challenge: lenses evaluated on every walk-around; MPI video audit (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. Every vehicle that arrives for service this week gets its headlight lenses evaluated during the walk-around. That's a shop standard now. Friday, you pull MPI videos and inspect them. Were the headlights addressed? Yes or no.

**Your move**
Set the standard Monday. Audit the videos Friday. Recognize the advisor who spotted it and shared it every time.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Idler Pulley Boost Meeting
title: Idler Pulley Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your idler pulley attach rate trails your serpentine belt jobs.
body_md:
**Bring**
A used idler pulley, if available; A photo or video MPI clip of a pulley spin test

**Word tracks**
- “My certified technician graded your drive belt system. The belt is worn, and the idler pulley is rough when he spins it. Here's the video. I'd like to do them together.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: idler pulley attach rate by advisor next to serpentine belt jobs
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: the belt rides on the pulleys; a worn bearing is noisy and chews up a new belt
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector spins the pulley on the photo or video MPI and shares what he hears and feels; vehicle's and Hector's voices
- 6:00 – The word track drill: drive belt system line, serpentine belt pairing, "just do the belt" objection
- 8:00 – The challenge: pulley grade and offer on every belt recommendation; you inspect the week's belt ROs Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, Hector picks the advisor who shared his pulley photos best, and that advisor's clip opens next week's meeting.

**Your move**
Run this meeting today. Inspect Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Nitrogen Inflation Boost Meeting
title: Nitrogen Inflation Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your nitrogen inflation attach rate trails your tire sales. Every new tire is a chance to offer it.
body_md:
**Bring**
Five recent ROs that include nitrogen; a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “Your left front was low when your vehicle came in. Let's set all four with nitrogen today, and your certified technician will check them again at your next visit.”
- “It is. What you're getting today is the service: all four set right and checked by your certified technician every visit.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the nitrogen inflation attach rate by advisor; a fill outside policy is a gap too
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Even wear and handling start with the right pressure; nitrogen keeps tire pressure more stable; dealership's voice (results may vary)
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector records all four pressures on the photo or video MPI
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Around the room, tire rotation pairing, the "air is free" response, deferred not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: Every fill on the RO per store policy; five ROs a day, inspect attach rate and gross Friday

**Inspect it**
Pull five ROs a day. Any fill that went out outside the policy gets a conversation the same day. Friday, you inspect the nitrogen attach rate AND the gross together.

**Your move**
Put ONE number on the board next to the nitrogen attach rate: nitrogen gross. What gets watched gets protected.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Oil Filter Boost Meeting
title: Oil Filter Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your own count shows 5,000-mile services going out the door without the right filter conversation.
body_md:
**Bring**
Five of today's 5,000-mile service ROs pulled for your spot check, a genuine oil filter, an aftermarket filter if you come across one.

**Word tracks**
- “Today we're replacing your oil filter with a genuine one made specifically for your engine — the same quality it left the factory with.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: two wins; your own five-RO capture check — genuine filter on every 5,000-mile service RO (manager-pick film, no screen number)
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: clean oil protects the engine between visits; manufacturer quality on every 5,000-mile service; dealership's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector captures the genuine filter on every RO; old filter on the photo or video MPI; parts keeps genuine filters staged
- 6:00 – The word track drill: genuine-filter line; engine air filter pairing; "is it necessary" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: five-RO capture check every day; perfect five inspected Friday earns lunch

**Inspect it**
Before the meeting, spot check five ROs from today. Verify that every 5,000-mile service RO has a genuine manufacturer oil filter captured. Then check the brand. If it's an aftermarket filter, that's your product knowledge conversation this week. You spot check five ROs every day this week. Not to catch anyone. To make it automatic.

**Your move**
Pull five ROs today, before anybody knows you're looking.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/PCV Valve Boost Meeting
title: PCV Valve Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your PCV valve attach rate falls below your best month, or your high-mileage engines are leaving without one.
body_md:
**Bring**
Three quiz questions on index cards, a used PCV valve if Hector has one.

**Word tracks**
- “Write it down. What does PCV stand for? What does it do? Which vehicles need it most?”
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends replacing your PCV valve.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: two wins; PCV valve attach rate by advisor from the screen; the three-question written quiz
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: positive crankcase ventilation; routes crankcase gases back to be burned; sticking valve, leaks, consumption, sludge
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector answers question three with your five-model list and grades the valve on the photo or video MPI; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector recommendation line; engine air filter pairing; deferred, not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: every graded PCV valve offered all week; re-quiz and five-MPI spot check Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, you run the same quiz, cold, and spot check five MPIs for the offer. Everybody gets three for three. Every day is a great day to teach before you inspect.

**Your move**
Print the cards tonight. Run the quiz Monday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Power Steering Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
title: Power Steering Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
workbook_title: Power Steering Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your power steering fluid exchange attach rate falls below your best month on the vehicles that still use fluid.
body_md:
**Bring**
A sample of dark used power steering fluid next to fresh.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends a power steering service.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: two wins; power steering fluid exchange attach rate by advisor from the screen; each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: heat and pressure break the fluid down; pump, rack, seals; how the wheel feels
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: quick reservoir check graded on the photo or video MPI; Hector verifies hydraulic, electric or electro-hydraulic; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line; groan-when-turning condition; topping-off response; deferred, not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: reservoir check on video at every major service all week; five MPIs Wednesday, five more inspected Friday

**Inspect it**
You spot check five MPIs Wednesday and five more Friday. Condition matters more than miles.

**Your move**
Know which of your common models have electric steering, so nobody quotes a vehicle that doesn't need it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Rear Wiper Blade Boost Meeting
title: Rear Wiper Blade Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your rear wiper blade attach rate trails your front blades. Every SUV and hatchback has one.
body_md:
**Bring**
Two or three recent photo or video MPI clips from vehicles with a rear wiper; a worn rear blade if the shop has one.

**Word tracks**
- “Your certified technician ran your rear wiper, and it's streaking right across the glass. Here's the video. Let's replace it while we're doing your front blades.”
- “Most people don't, until it's snowing and they're backing out of the driveway.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the rear wiper blade attach rate by advisor; do the math with your own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Conditions language; the rear glass in a snowy driveway
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Main-line techs in the room: Hector runs it, watches it, grades it, videos it; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Advisor and tech pairs with a real video, front wiper blades pairing, the "never use it" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: Rear wiper graded on video on every applicable MPI; three random MPIs a day, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Pull three MPIs a day at random. If the rear wiper isn't graded, that tech hears about it, kindly, the same day. Friday, you inspect the week with techs and advisors together.

**Your move**
Find ONE certified technician who gets it right every time, and thank them in front of the whole shop.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Rotors Front Boost Meeting
title: Rotors Front Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your front rotor attach rate trails your front pad jobs.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE used front rotor from the bench, if your certified technicians have one; A photo or video MPI clip showing a rotor measurement

**Word tracks**
- “My certified technician graded your front rotors and measured them. Here's the video. They're near the end of their life, and that makes this urgent.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: front rotor attach rate by advisor; each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: pulsation, grooving, glazing; fresh pads seat poorly on worn rotors
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: rotor measurement plus photo or video on every MPI; percentage of life left: plenty left is proactive, near the end is urgent; Hector's voice; percentage of life left with proactive and urgent examples; your measurements and equipment set the numbers
- 6:00 – The word track drill: graded-and-measured line, front pads pairing, "can't you just reuse them?" objection
- 8:00 – The challenge: measurement on every MPI all week; you pull ten MPIs at random and inspect Friday

**Your move**
Put the measurement standard on the board today. Inspect it Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Rotors Rear Boost Meeting
title: Rotors Rear Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your rear rotor attach rate trails your rear pad jobs.
body_md:
**Bring**
A photo or video MPI clip of a rear rotor measurement; A whiteboard split into two columns: rear pads and rear rotors

**Word tracks**
- “My certified technician graded your rear brakes. The pads are low, and the rotors measured below where your manufacturer wants them. I'd like to do the complete brake job so you only pay for this once.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: rear rotor attach rate by advisor against rear pad jobs; do the math with your own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: new pads need a true surface; pads-only comebacks
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: measure and show rear rotors on the photo or video MPI; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: complete brake job line, rear pads pairing, "just do the pads" objection, deferred not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: rotor measurement and complete brake offer on every rear pad recommendation; you inspect the rear brake ROs Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, you pull the week's rear brake ROs and inspect every one for the measurement and the offer. Watch the gap close.

**Your move**
Run this meeting today. Inspect the rear brake ROs Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Serpentine Belt Boost Meeting
title: Serpentine Belt Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your serpentine belt attach rate falls below your best month, or Hector's belt photos aren't reaching the customer.
body_md:
**Bring**
A used serpentine belt with micro-cracking (ask Hector to bring one); A photo or video MPI clip of a belt inspection; Your belt wear gauge, if your shop has one

**Word tracks**
- “I hear you. Today's belts don't crack like they used to. They wear down like tire tread. My certified technician graded yours, and here's the video of the ribs.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: serpentine belt attach rate by advisor; do the math with your own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: pass the used belt around; ribs wear like tire tread even when the outside looks fine
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: every belt graded, photo or video of the ribs up close; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: "my belt looks fine" role play, idler pulley pairing
- 8:00 – The challenge: rib photo or video on every belt recommendation; you check five belt ROs Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, you check five belt ROs. The advisor with the best video clip gets it shown at next week's huddle.

**Your move**
Ask Hector for that belt today. Run the drill tomorrow morning.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Spark Plugs Boost Meeting
title: Spark Plugs Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your spark plug attach rate falls below your best month, or vehicles at their plug interval are leaving without the conversation.
body_md:
**Bring**
A used set of spark plugs next to a new plug, if available; Your write-up checklist; Your parts department partner with the plug type and interval sheet for the top models in your lanes

**Word tracks**
- “Your vehicle is at the mileage where your manufacturer schedules spark plugs. Here's what that does for your engine, and here's what worn ones look like.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: spark plug attach rate by advisor; do the math with your own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: parts department guest on plug type and interval; rough idle, hard starts, slipping fuel economy; manufacturer's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: worn plug next to a new plug on the photo or video MPI
- 6:00 – The word track drill: model call-out quick-fire, manufacturer schedule line, tank additive pairing
- 8:00 – The challenge: plug interval on the write-up checklist; you pop-quiz three advisors on three models Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, you pop-quiz three advisors on three models. Celebrate the ones who nail it.

**Your move**
Book your parts partner today. Update the checklist before the meeting.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/TPMS Service Boost Meeting
title: TPMS Service Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your TPMS service attach rate trails your tire jobs. And on the first cold morning of fall, when the lights come on.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your tire rotation checklist; a stack of yesterday's rotation ROs; a used tire pressure sensor if the shop has one.

**Word tracks**
- “Your certified technician tested all four tire pressure sensors. Your left rear is approaching end of life. Since the wheels are already off for your rotation, let's replace it today.”
- “That's the point. We caught it before your light did.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the TPMS service attach rate by advisor; count sensor inspections on yesterday's rotation ROs
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Sensors reach end of life; the light comes on at the worst time
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Sensor inspection is a standard checklist line; Hector records every sensor on the photo or video MPI; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Around the room, tire rotation pairing, the "my light's not on" response, deferred not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: Every rotation RO includes a sensor inspection; daily pull of yesterday's ROs, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Every morning, pull yesterday's rotation ROs. If the sensor inspection isn't there, it gets fixed that day, with Hector and the advisor together. Friday, you inspect the whole week.

**Your move**
Walk into the shop and ask ONE certified technician to show you their last sensor inspection. Then thank them.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Tank Additive Boost Meeting
title: Tank Additive Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your tank additive attach rate falls below your best month. It's the first rung of the fuel ladder, and it belongs on every visit that qualifies.
body_md:
**Bring**
A bottle of tank additive to pass around; a photo or video MPI clip of a drivability grade.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends a tank additive today. It keeps cleaning your fuel system between visits.”
- “Good fuel helps. This keeps your fuel system cleaning between visits.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: tank additive attach rate by advisor (on screen); each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: keeps cleaning between visits; maintenance in a bottle; dealership's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector shows drivability conditions on the photo or video MPI
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line, fuel injector clean pairing, "premium gas" objection; the fuel ladder — one-part, two-part, complete
- 8:00 – The challenge: tank additive as the first yes on every 5,000-mile service (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. Track it as a streak. Every day an advisor offers tank additive on every 5,000-mile service, their square gets a mark. Friday, you check the ROs behind the marks.

**Your move**
Set the standard Monday. Check the ROs Friday. Recognize the advisor who offered it every time, and coach the one who skipped it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Throttle Body Clean Boost Meeting
title: Throttle Body Clean Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your throttle body clean attach rate trails your engine air filter replacements.
body_md:
**Bring**
A before-and-after photo or video of a dirty throttle body; A used engine air filter

**Word tracks**
- “Since we're replacing your engine air filter, I'd like to clean the throttle body right behind it. The filter catches most of the debris, not all of it. Here's the photo.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: throttle body clean attach rate by advisor next to engine air filter replacements
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: the air filter is not perfect; deposits behind it can mean rough idle or sluggish response; vehicle's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: recommend it with every engine air filter, before-and- after photo or video
- 6:00 – The word track drill: right-behind-the-filter line, engine air filter and tank additive pairings, "it runs fine" objection; tank additive is the one-part fuel service
- 8:00 – The challenge: offer on every engine air filter replacement; you inspect those ROs Friday

**Your move**
Announce the standard today. Inspect the filter ROs Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Timing Belt Boost Meeting
title: Timing Belt Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your timing belt attach rate falls below your best month, or vehicles at their timing belt interval are leaving without the conversation.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your outreach list from the customer database, split by advisor; A used timing belt, if your certified technicians have one

**Word tracks**
- “Your vehicle is right at the mileage where your manufacturer schedules the timing belt. I'd love to get you in before that becomes urgent.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: timing belt attach rate by advisor; hold up the outreach list
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: a scheduled replacement per your manufacturer; on many engines a failure can damage the engine; manufacturer's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: mileage checked against the manufacturer's schedule, visible belt graded on photo or video
- 6:00 – The word track drill: outreach call practice, water pump pairing, "it's running fine" objection
- 8:00 – The challenge: every name on the list gets a call or letter; you inspect the slices and count appointments Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, you check every slice and count the appointments set. Celebrate the leader.

**Your move**
Pull the list today. Hand it out tomorrow.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Tire Balance Boost Meeting
title: Tire Balance Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your tire balance attach rate falls below your best month, or customers are describing a vibration at highway speed.
body_md:
**Bring**
A jar for the drawing and name slips; a photo or video MPI clip showing uneven tread wear.

**Word tracks**
