- “When your tires are out of balance, you're essentially bouncing down the road. That's okay sometimes, but not when it rains.”
- “Your certified technician graded uneven wear on your tread. Let's balance your tires today so they roll smooth and wear evenly.”
- “A lot of times you won't at first. The tread shows it before the steering wheel does, and you'll feel it most on wet roads.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the tire balance attach rate by advisor; reward at forecast, then accelerators
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Out of balance means bouncing down the road, and not when it rains; vehicle's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector notes vibration and uneven wear on the photo or video MPI; the balancer simulates highway speeds, down to the quarter ounce (results may vary based on your equipment)
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Around the room, tire rotation pairing, the "no vibration" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: First and Last drawing each day; inspect the week's balance ROs Friday and draw for lunch

**Inspect it**
Every name goes in the jar. Friday afternoon, you inspect the week's balance ROs, then draw for a free lunch.

**Your move**
Announce the first and last sellers every single day. Out loud. On the drive. Visibility is the whole game.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Tire Pressure Check Boost Meeting
title: Tire Pressure Check Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your own count shows cars leaving without a pressure check. And on the first cold morning of fall.
body_md:
**Bring**
A printed post-service checklist with tire pressure added; a tire gauge.

**Word tracks**
- “My certified technician Hector graded your tire pressures and set them to your manufacturer's spec. Your left rear was low compared to the right. Here's the video. That's a sign we should check for a slow leak or your tire pressure sensor.”
- “That's good news. The video shows the reading, and we caught this one early.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: your own count — five ROs per advisor, how many show tire pressure verified out the door; the gaps lead to the real conversations
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: grip, stopping, tire life; conditions, not opinions
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: every tire graded and recorded on the photo or video MPI; same-axle difference is an immediate notification; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: graded-pressures line, TPMS service pairing, "my light's not on" objection
- 8:00 – The challenge: daily first-and-last RO check all week (inspect Friday)

**Inspect it**
Last — the challenge. First-and-last check, all week. Every day, you inspect the first RO and the last RO out the door. Is the pressure recorded? Is any same-axle difference noted and shared? Friday, you review the week.

**Your move**
Put tire pressure on the post-service checklist tomorrow. Friday, recognize the tech-and-advisor pair that caught the most.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Tire Rotation Boost Meeting
title: Tire Rotation Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your tire rotation attach rate falls below your best month, or 5,000-mile services are leaving without one.
body_md:
**Bring**
A tread depth gauge; a few recent photo or video MPI clips showing tread measurements.

**Word tracks**
- “While we're doing your 5,000-mile service, let's rotate your tires so they wear evenly.”
- “Your fronts measured lower than your rears. The fronts do the steering and most of the braking. Rotating evens that out so the whole set lasts longer.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the tire rotation attach rate by advisor; no rotations means the question is not being asked
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Fronts steer and brake, so they wear faster; rotation evens it out
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector measures all four corners with color on the photo or video MPI; fronts next to rears; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Quick lane first, tire balance and wheel alignment pairings (rotate every service, balance every other, align every third), the "they look fine" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: Every 5,000-mile service gets the rotation offer; five ROs a day, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Every advisor shares the tread measurements with every customer. Spot check five ROs a day. Friday, you inspect the rotation attach rate by advisor.

**Your move**
Stand in your quick lane for ONE hour and listen. Effort is easy to hear.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Tire Sealant Boost Meeting
title: Tire Sealant Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your tire sealant attach rate trails your tire sales, or before road-trip season.
body_md:
**Bring**
A bottle of tire sealant with the label turned away; a photo or video MPI clip of an empty spare tire well.

**Word tracks**
- “Your vehicle doesn't carry a spare tire. Here's the video. Tire sealant is there for a small puncture, so you're not stuck waiting on the side of the road.”
- “That's great. And with sealant, you might not have to wait for them.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the tire sealant attach rate by advisor next to today's no-spare count
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Many vehicles leave the factory with no spare; customers learn it on the shoulder
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector notes spare or no spare on every MPI; video of the empty well; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Around the room, tire rotation pairing, the roadside assistance response
- 8:00 – The challenge: Spare recorded on every MPI and every no-spare gets the conversation; count vehicles vs offers daily, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Start each morning huddle with the same question. Count the no-spare vehicles. Count the offers at the end of the day. Friday, you inspect the gap between the two.

**Your move**
Ask the question every morning, and let your team find the answer themselves.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Transfer Case Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
title: Transfer Case Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
workbook_title: Transfer Case Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your transfer case fluid exchange attach rate falls below your best month. And every fall, before four-wheel-drive season.
body_md:
**Bring**
A sample of old transfer case fluid saved by a certified technician; a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “Your vehicle has TWO driveline fluids — differential AND transfer case. Your transfer case fluid has done its job. Let's replace it with fluid validated for your AWD system.”
- “This fluid ages with time and heat, not just miles. Let's look at how you use the truck.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the transfer case fluid exchange attach rate by advisor; do the math with your own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: The traffic cop for power; towing, off-road, snow and water age the fluid
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades the fluid and shows it on the photo or video MPI; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Around the room, differential fluid exchange pairing, the "I don't drive much" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: Every all-wheel and four-wheel drive differential exchange gets the transfer case conversation; five ROs a day, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Spot check five ROs a day. Friday, you inspect the transfer case attach rate with the whole team.

**Your move**
Put the differential and transfer case attach rates side by side on your board. When they move together, your team is having the full conversation.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Transmission Filter Boost Meeting
title: Transmission Filter Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your transmission filter attach rate trails your transmission fluid exchanges. They should travel together.
body_md:
**Bring**
A used transmission filter Hector pulls and brings to the meeting.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends a transmission service — fluid and filter together.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: two wins; transmission filter attach rate by advisor from the screen; each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: pass the used filter around; what it catches is the whole story; fresh fluid through a clogged filter defeats the service
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades fluid and filter on equipped vehicles; bright versus dark on the photo or video MPI; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line; transmission fluid exchange pairing; "just the fluid" response; deferred, not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: filter conversation on every equipped transmission fluid exchange; every transmission RO inspected Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, every advisor brings their best filter conversation on video, and the team picks the one you play Monday.

**Your move**
Ask Hector for that filter today. Pass it around Monday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Transmission Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
title: Transmission Fluid Exchange Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your transmission fluid exchange attach rate falls below your best month, and again before towing and road-trip season.
body_md:
**Bring**
A sample of bright fresh transmission fluid, a sample of dark used fluid, one photo or video MPI clip of the fluid.

**Word tracks**
- “Based on time, mileage and condition of your vehicle, my certified technician Hector recommends a transmission service.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: two wins; transmission fluid exchange attach rate by advisor from the screen; each advisor does the math with their own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: power to the wheels; heat is the enemy; the watch picture
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector shows the fluid on the photo or video MPI; confirms automatic, CVT, dual-clutch or EV gearbox; manufacturer's voice vs Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Hector line; lifetime-fluid and topping-off responses; transmission filter pairing; deferred, not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: fluid on video for every transmission recommendation all week; every transmission RO inspected Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, you pull every transmission RO and inspect each one for the video.

**Your move**
Set the two fluid samples on the counter Monday and put the lifetime objection to bed.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Washer Fluid Top-Off Boost Meeting
title: Washer Fluid Top-Off Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your count shows empty reservoirs, and before winter and bug season.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your post-service checklist; a jug of washer fluid; a photo or video MPI clip showing a low reservoir.

**Word tracks**
- “Your washer fluid was low, so your certified technician topped it off. Your windshield will clear the next time you need it.”
- “Little things are the things customers remember. Share every one of them.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: your own count — five ROs per advisor, how many mention the washer fluid top-off; charged or not, every unmentioned top-off is a missed moment
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: A low reservoir is a condition; the mention is the marketing
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Checklist line: Hector checks, tops off and notes it on the photo or video MPI; dealership's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Delivery word track around the room, the advisor's "too small" objection, front wiper blades pairing
- 8:00 – The challenge: Every RO shows the check and every delivery the mention; five ROs a day plus delivery listening, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Pull five ROs at random each day. Walk the drive at delivery twice a day and listen for it. Friday, you inspect the checklist with the team.

**Your move**
Catch ONE advisor making the mention, and recognize them in front of the team.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Water Pump Boost Meeting
title: Water Pump Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your water pump attach rate trails your timing belt jobs on the engines where they share the labor.
body_md:
**Bring**
A used water pump, if your certified technicians have one; A photo or video MPI clip of pump seepage

**Word tracks**
- “Since we're already in there for your timing belt, I'd like to replace the water pump at the same time. You'll only pay that labor once.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: water pump attach rate by advisor next to timing belt jobs
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: on many engines the pump sits behind the timing belt; the labor is already being done
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades seepage, weep hole residue and bearing play on photo or video; Hector's voice
- 6:00 – The word track drill: pay-the-labor-once line, timing belt and coolant exchange pairing, "not leaking" objection
- 8:00 – The challenge: documented water pump discussion on every timing belt RO; you pull every timing belt RO Friday

**Inspect it**
Friday, you pull every timing belt RO. Every one shows the discussion.

**Your move**
Announce the standard today. Inspect Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Wheel Alignment Boost Meeting
title: Wheel Alignment Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your wheel alignment attach rate falls below your best month, after pothole season, or with every new set of tires.
body_md:
**Bring**
A recent before-and-after alignment printout; a photo or video MPI clip showing inside- edge wear.

**Word tracks**
- “Your inside edges are wearing faster than the rest of the tread. Let's align it today so your tires wear evenly and last.”
- “The tire shows it before the steering wheel does. Here's the video of your inside edge.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the wheel alignment attach rate by advisor; reward at forecast, then accelerators
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Conditions: pulls, off-center wheel, inside-edge wear; vehicle's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector shows the wear pattern on the photo or video MPI; before-and-after printout to the advisor; laser precision (degree may vary by equipment)
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Around the room, tire rotation and tire balance pairings (rotate every service, balance every other, align every third), the "drives straight" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: Alignment offer on every vehicle due on your schedule; five ROs a day, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
If your shop doesn't have a machine, the schedule still stands, so remind the team of it. Spot check five ROs a day. Friday, you inspect the alignment attach rate by advisor.

**Your move**
Hand ONE advisor a before-and-after printout and let them share it on their next alignment offer.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Windshield Treatment Boost Meeting
title: Windshield Treatment Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your windshield treatment attach rate trails your wiper sales. And right before your rainy season.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your team's piggyback pairing list; a spray bottle of water for the glass demo.

**Word tracks**
- “New blades work best on clean, treated glass. Let's add the windshield treatment today so rain beads up and rolls right off.”
- “It helps water bead up and roll off the glass, so you can see better in the rain, even before the wipers kick in.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the windshield treatment attach rate by advisor next to wiper sales; do the math with your own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: Pick the pairing off the piggyback list and share ONE feature and benefit: rain beads up and rolls off; dealership's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector shows the glass on the photo or video MPI: water, one swipe, smear or not
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Around the room, front wiper blades pairing, the "what does that even do" response
- 8:00 – The challenge: Treatment offer on every wiper sale; five wiper ROs a day, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Thursday, a two-minute role play. Every advisor sells you a pair of wipers and the treatment, cold. Friday, you inspect the windshield treatment attach rate with the team.

**Your move**
Next week, pick the next pairing off the list and run the same play.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Op Code Boost Meetings/10 mins/Wiper Inserts Boost Meeting
title: Wiper Inserts Boost Meeting
best_used_for: Any week your wiper insert attach rate falls below your best month, or you're losing wiper sales to price.
body_md:
**Bring**
A worn wiper insert next to a new one; a whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “Your wiper frames are in good shape, but the rubber is streaking. We can replace just the inserts today so you can see clearly again.”
- “It can. I'll note it on your record so we look at it again next visit.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two positives, then the number: Two positives, then the wiper insert attach rate by advisor; do the math with your own average ticket
- 2:00 – The customer WHY: The insert is the rubber that touches the glass; cracked, streaking, hazing; vehicle's voice
- 4:00 – The certified technician's part: Hector grades the insert, not just the frame, on the photo or video MPI
- 6:00 – The word track drill: Worn and new insert around the room, windshield treatment pairing, deferred not declined
- 8:00 – The challenge: Frame-or-insert question on every wiper conversation; inserts on their own board line; five ROs a day, inspect Friday

**Inspect it**
Inserts get their own line on the board, by advisor. Spot check five ROs a day. Friday, you inspect the insert line with the team.

**Your move**
Catch ONE advisor offering inserts the right way, and put their name on the board first.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/15 plus mins/Script Rewriting Protocol — Build Two Versions and Time Both
title: Script Rewriting Protocol — Build Two Versions and Time Both
workbook_title: Script Rewriting Protocol — Build Two Versions and Time Both
best_used_for: Anytime your BDC rewrites a script. A new campaign launch. A script that's stopped booking.
body_md:
**Bring**
The current script, a stopwatch, and a whiteboard; block 30–45 minutes.

**Word tracks**
- “The goal is to match the original time, or run ten percent shorter. If it got longer, we cut until it doesn't.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Time the original script out loud; write the ceiling on the board
- 5:00 – Build version one (full word tracks) and version two (bullets)
- 20:00 – Time both; cut together until they match the original or run 10% shorter
- 30:00 – Pair practice: full version, then bullets, swap roles, re-time
- 40:00 – Launch both; set the end-of-week call review (five recorded calls per caller)

**Your move**
Grab the script your team rewrote most recently. Time it against the original. If it grew, schedule this meeting. *Academy: SMA 120 Language and Process Standards (weeks 9–12); revisited in SMA 110*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/15 plus mins/The 73-Second Pitch — Time Your Speech
title: The 73-Second Pitch — Time Your Speech
situation_tags: Phones and BDC|Attach rate or ticket flat
best_used_for: Your advisors are calling customers with inspection results and the close rate is soft.
body_md:
**Bring**
A stopwatch, ONE sample RO with a recommended item, and every advisor's personal phone for recording.

**Word tracks**
- “I'm not grading your personality. I'm grading the clock. Under sixty, you're rushing the customer. Over two minutes, you're losing them. Let's land it in the window.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Set the benchmark: the complete pitch lives in the 60–90 second window
- 3:00 – Manager delivers the full pitch live while someone times it
- 6:00 – Each advisor records the pitch on their own phone; time every recording
- 14:00 – Play back and diagnose: under a minute = skipped pieces, over two = rambling
- 20:00 – Re-record until every advisor lands in the window; set the live-call spot check

**Your move**
Pick ONE live call per advisor. Stand close enough to hear it. Time it. Coach the gap the same day.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/5-15 mins/Incoming Phone Call Tips
title: Incoming Phone Call Tips
situation_tags: Phones and BDC|New hire or onboarding
best_used_for: Phone surveys are slipping, reservations are getting lost, or you've got new advisors on the phones.
body_md:
**Bring**
The thirteen elements of a healthy incoming call on the board; phones or a quiet spot for role play.

**Word tracks**
- “A customer books a 9:00 reservation, then says, 'I'll just drop it off at 7:30 before work.' What do you say?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Thirteen elements on the board
- 2:00 – Enthusiasm and active listening
- 4:00 – Repeat your name after introductions
- 6:00 – The 7:30 drop-off question and the redirect line
- 8:00 – Paired role play of the full call, then swap
- 13:00 – Set up the ONE-bullet-a-day mini-meeting rotation

**Your move**
Run the full list once. Then pick ONE bullet a day for a two-minute mini-meeting until your team owns all thirteen.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/5-15 mins/Phone Tips for the Angry Customer
title: Phone Tips for the Angry Customer
workbook_title: Phone Tips for the Angry Customer
best_used_for: After a rough call. After a rough week. Or before either one shows up.
body_md:
**Bring**
The seven steps written on the dry erase board (or nothing; it can be a conversation).

**Word tracks**
- “Here's the line I want every one of you using: 'I'm sorry you're unhappy with the wait. Let me see what I can do about that.'”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Frame: everyone gets the angry call; seven steps on the board
- 1:00 – Steps 1–4: listen, summarize in their words, be agreeable, sympathize
- 5:00 – Steps 5–7: apologize (the line), fix it or find who can, follow up
- 9:00 – Room check: last angry call, which steps hit / skipped
- 12:00 – Close: 'I'm with you'; follow-up-within-a-day standard

**Your move**
Leave the seven on the board. Every angry call gets a follow-up within a day, and you check that it happened.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/5-15 mins/Track Reservations Set, Kept, and Best Show Percentage
title: Track Reservations Set, Kept, and Best Show Percentage
workbook_title: Track Reservations Set, Kept, and Best Show Percentage
best_used_for: Monthly BDC review. Or anytime the appointment board looks full and the drive doesn't.
body_md:
**Bring**
Reservations set and reservations kept by BDC advisor for the last 30 days.

**Word tracks**
- “The gap between set and kept is where our revenue leaks. Every no-show is a customer we already won, and then lost.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Put up the three numbers by BDC advisor; two positives (top setter, top keeper)
- 3:00 – Find the gap between set and kept
- 5:00 – Diagnose: high set / low keep = confirmation cadence and pre-arrival communication
- 8:00 – Role-play ONE confirmation call modeled by the best keeper
- 11:00 – Each BDC advisor sets a two-week show-percentage goal; post and track daily

**Your move**
Pull set and kept by advisor. Find the biggest gap. Have the confirmation conversation with that ONE person.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/5-15 mins/Use Technology to Personalize the Reason for Calling
title: Use Technology to Personalize the Reason for Calling
workbook_title: Use Technology to Personalize the Reason for Calling
best_used_for: Your outbound appointment calls sound like everybody else's. Due by calendar. Mass list. Nobody calls back.
body_md:
**Bring**
Tomorrow's outbound call list (ten customers), access to your manufacturer's connected vehicle app or telematics data, and a phone on speaker.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Inventory the connected vehicle data your store already has
- 2:00 – Pull ten customers from today's list and review their vehicle data
- 4:00 – Old opener vs. new opener: rewrite the reason for calling
- 6:00 – Live calls in the room with the new opener, quick feedback after each
- 12:00 – Set the standard: connected data in every outbound call reason

**Your move**
Pull tomorrow's call list. Find every vehicle reporting data. Those calls open with the vehicle, not the calendar.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/"Questions, Comments, Concerns?" — The Three-Part Close
title: "Questions, Comments, Concerns?" — The Three-Part Close
situation_tags: Phones and BDC|Language and word tracks|Upset customers
best_used_for: Customers approve on the phone and then push back at pickup. Surprises at the cashier. Survey comments you never saw coming.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing.

**Word tracks**
- “Before we hang up — do you have any questions, comments, or concerns?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The problem with 'any questions?'
- 1:00 – Teach the three doors: questions, comments, concerns
- 2:00 – Paired role play: customer with a hidden concern; swap
- 4:00 – Standard: all three words on every call

**Your move**
Stand within earshot of ONE call per advisor per day. Listen for the close. Count the doors.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/'I Got You' — Reassurance Plus Action in Three Words
title: 'I Got You' — Reassurance Plus Action in Three Words
workbook_title: 'I Got You' — Reassurance Plus Action in Three Words
situation_tags: Phones and BDC|Upset customers|Language and word tracks
best_used_for: Customers are calling back frustrated, or you're hearing "I'll look into it" on the phone way too often.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing. Optional: a few real customer concerns from this week to use in the drill.

**Word tracks**
- “'I got you' is only half the sentence. The other half is the action. Reassurance plus action — every time.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Teach: reassurance plus action
- 1:00 – Model the lines
- 2:00 – Round-robin concern drill (action + time)
- 4:00 – Standard: retire "I'll look into it"; five-call check

**Your move**
Listen to five customer calls. Count every "I got you" — and check that something actually happened after it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/Active Listening Practice
title: Active Listening Practice
situation_tags: Phones and BDC|Language and word tracks|One-on-one coaching
best_used_for: Any day. Bonus points if there's a policy nobody's following — use THAT as your script. Or use your phone script. You coach the skill and the policy in the same two minutes.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE policy that isn't being followed, or your phone script; the three customer statements.

**Word tracks**
- “Thanks for giving me a few minutes. I appreciate you being a great leader on this team. I've got ONE item today — active listening. I'm going to give you three customer statements. Listen, and respond.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Thank the advisor; name the ONE item
- 0:20 – Statement one: name, concern, ONE pertinent fact
- 0:50 – Statement two: loyalty, the Saturday, deferred items
- 1:20 – Statement three: apology, immediate update, never on hold
- 1:50 – Praise ONE specific thing they did well

**Your move**
Pick ONE policy or your phone script, grab ONE advisor in the hallway, and run all three statements.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/An Ounce of Prevention Beats a Pound of Cure — Planning Principle
title: An Ounce of Prevention Beats a Pound of Cure — Planning Principle
workbook_title: An Ounce of Prevention Beats a Pound of Cure — Planning Principle
situation_tags: Phones and BDC|Objections and deferred work
best_used_for: Your advisors are improvising on the phone. Fumbling for a document. Hearing an objection and freezing.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE RO from the rack to plan out loud; a five-point planning card (hand, send, analogy, objection, piggyback) is optional.

**Word tracks**
- “Before you pick up that phone, I want thirty seconds. Hand, send, analogy, objection, piggyback. Plan it, then dial.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Open with the Franklin line and the 30-seconds-vs-30-minutes math
- 1:00 – Teach the five things to plan before every call
- 2:00 – Model it: manager plans ONE RO out loud in 30 seconds
- 3:00 – Drill: each advisor plans their next call out loud
- 4:30 – Set the standard: no call without the 30-second plan

**Your move**
Walk the drive twice before lunch. Catch ONE advisor reaching for the phone and have them run their five for you. If they've got it, let them dial.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/Call Logs
title: Call Logs
best_used_for: Mid-month, once your initiatives are launched and running. Works for a BDC or a team of advisors.
body_md:
**Bring**
Call logs spot-checked before the meeting, a small golden log trophy, a gift card or free lunch for the best phone-generated job; monthly: an axe trophy.

**Word tracks**
- “This log goes to you. Every call, every name, every callback. Documented. That's how nothing falls through the cracks.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Present the Golden Log to the best call-log user (public, big deal)
- 0:45 – Reward the advisor whose phone call produced a big job (gift card or free lunch)
- 1:30 – Monthly only: award the axe to the advisor who logged the most customers
- 2:00 – Back to work

**Inspect it**
What to bring: The call logs, spot-checked before the meeting. A small golden log trophy. A gift card or a free lunch.

**Your move**
Spot-check every advisor's call log. Order the Golden Log. Present it in front of the whole team.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/Enthusiasm Mini-Meeting
title: Enthusiasm Mini-Meeting
best_used_for: The phones are ringing and your team treats every call like a burden. Or the energy on the drive is just flat.
body_md:
**Bring**
A couple of numbers from your phone logs (how many callers showed up) and one short inspirational story in your pocket.

**Word tracks**
- “Describe something you did recently that made you happy.”
- “That feeling right there? That's what I want you to have when the next customer drives in. Or the next time the phone rings.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Acknowledge the work: two specific positives
- 0:30 – Phone stats: how many logged callers showed up; recount a money story from following the phone script
- 1:15 – Make them smile: advisor describes a recent happy moment (redo if no smile)
- 1:45 – Deliver the line: 'That feeling is what I want you to have when the next customer drives in'

**Your move**
Pick ONE advisor. Two positives. One phone stat. One smile. Two minutes.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/Memorable Greeting
title: Memorable Greeting
situation_tags: Phones and BDC|Language and word tracks
best_used_for: An advisor's calls sound rushed. Name tossed off at the top, gone by the end.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing. Just two sincere compliments for the advisor.

**Word tracks**
- “Before we start, thank you for your hard work lately, and for being a leader on this team. ONE quick item: when someone calls in, are you introducing yourself in a memorable, valuable way?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Two nice things about the advisor
- 0:20 – The question, then the average greeting
- 0:40 – Three better greetings: guiding, help, thank you
- 1:20 – The steer: status update or reservation?
- 1:40 – Advisor says the new greeting out loud twice

**Your move**
Pick ONE advisor. Two nice things, three greetings, ONE steer. Two minutes. Then listen to their next call.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/Pre-Call Prep — Read the RO Before You Dial
title: Pre-Call Prep — Read the RO Before You Dial
workbook_title: Pre-Call Prep — Read the RO Before You Dial
situation_tags: New hire or onboarding|Phones and BDC
best_used_for: New advisor training. And anytime you hear an MPI call that sounds like a guess.
body_md:
**Bring**
A few open ROs with completed MPIs.

**Word tracks**
- “Before you dial, you answer all of these without looking. If you can't, you're not ready to call. Read the RO first.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Set the standard: the pre-call questions
- 1:00 – Drill: 30 seconds with an RO, flip it, answer every question
- 3:00 – Around the room until everyone has been quizzed
- 4:30 – Set the inspection: three pre-dial spot checks a day

**Your move**
Three spot checks a day. Ask the question before the dial. Watch the yeses climb.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Phones and the BDC/Under 5 mins/The Buddy System — Pair Advisors for Emergency Coverage
title: The Buddy System — Pair Advisors for Emergency Coverage
workbook_title: The Buddy System — Pair Advisors for Emergency Coverage
best_used_for: Any time your voicemail greetings send customers nowhere.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your advisor pairings (overlapping shifts) worked out before the meeting.

**Word tracks**
- “Starting today, everybody has a buddy. If your customer has an emergency and can't reach you, your buddy takes care of them.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The dead-end voicemail story
- 1:00 – Announce the buddy pairs
- 2:00 – Each advisor adds the buddy line to their greeting
- 3:00 – Record greetings before leaving the room
- 4:30 – You'll call every line this week to check

**Your move**
Pair them Monday. Greetings recorded in the meeting. Spot check every line by Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Prospecting/15 plus mins/Community Discounts
title: Community Discounts
best_used_for: You want new customers on the drive — and you want your advisors thinking like owners.
body_md:
**Bring**
A one-sheeter savings plan, a dedicated tracking op code, and ONE local contact name (school, civic club, chamber, hospital) per advisor.

**Word tracks**
- “You're not just a service advisor. You're a small business. This is your book of business — go build it.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The second circle: your community
- 3:00 – Hand each advisor a different organization and contact name
- 7:00 – Hand out the one-sheeter and the tracking op code
- 10:00 – Announce the incentive
- 13:00 – Each advisor writes a three-step plan on the board
- 18:00 – Set the two-week check-in

**Your move**
Make the first introduction yourself. ONE phone call to ONE school, with your advisor sitting next to you — then hand them the ball. *Academy: Term 2 boost track, about 5 a week (weeks 13–24); Practicum 2*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Prospecting/5-15 mins/Friends and Family Discounts
title: Friends and Family Discounts
best_used_for: Your appointment board has holes. Drive traffic is light. You need opportunities — not someday. Today.
body_md:
**Bring**
A one-page list of today's discounts (windshield replacements, body shop visits, routine maintenance, friends and family) with the amounts you set.

**Word tracks**
- “Before we prospect anyone else, we prospect us. Your car, your family's car, your best friend's car. This discount is for them — today.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Prospecting starts with you and your team
- 2:00 – Announce today's discounts
- 5:00 – Each team member writes three names to share the offer with
- 9:00 – Names on the board; track appointments next to them
- 12:00 – Set tomorrow's follow-up

**Your move**
Put the friends and family offer on every advisor's desk and track every appointment it books. Celebrate the first one at the next huddle.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Prospecting/5-15 mins/Introduce the New Vehicle Buyer to the Service Team
title: Introduce the New Vehicle Buyer to the Service Team
workbook_title: Introduce the New Vehicle Buyer to the Service Team
best_used_for: Start of the month, or any time first-visit retention looks soft.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your list of recent new vehicle deliveries.

**Word tracks**
- “Every new vehicle buyer gets physically walked over to a service advisor before they leave. Every one. My advisors will be ready.”
- “On every delivery, before the customer leaves, ask about every other vehicle in the household — and get it on the schedule.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Review recent new vehicle deliveries and first-visit return
- 2:00 – Track ONE: the ask to the sales manager; assign an advisor of the day for introductions
- 5:00 – Track TWO: advisor huddle on household prospecting at active delivery
- 10:00 – Set the weekly inspection: three deliveries, what did we learn about the household

**Your move**
Make the ask with sales — or start the household standard on your drive. Either way, bridge the gap.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Prospecting/5-15 mins/Knock, Knock, Knock — Prospecting Beyond the Drive
title: Knock, Knock, Knock — Prospecting Beyond the Drive
workbook_title: Knock, Knock, Knock — Prospecting Beyond the Drive
situation_tags: Start of month|Slow traffic or prospecting
best_used_for: Early in the month. Traffic's soft. Or you want your team thinking like owners instead of waiting on the Up Bus.
body_md:
**Bring**
A restaurant-worker tracking code set up in your DMS, a one-sheeter with the restaurant-worker discount, written bonus rules (50-mile and same-household), and the name of a friendly nearby dealer of another make.

**Word tracks**
- “Every restaurant-worker customer you write up — come get me. I want to meet them personally.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Frame it: customers are everywhere; reference Friends and Family Discounts and Community Discounts
- 2:00 – Launch the restaurant-worker offer: discount, 10% commission bump, manager meets every one of those customers
- 5:00 – Share the friendly-dealer recall/warranty swap
- 7:00 – Announce the 50-mile bonus and the same-household prize with a date range
- 10:00 – Each advisor names ONE restaurant or business they'll prospect this week

**Your move**
Set up the restaurant-worker tracking code, post the bonus rules, and meet every one of those customers yourself.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Prospecting/5-15 mins/The Lapsed Customer Call — Bring Them Back
title: The Lapsed Customer Call — Bring Them Back
workbook_title: The Lapsed Customer Call — Bring Them Back
situation_tags: Slow traffic or prospecting|Phones and BDC|Objections and deferred work
best_used_for: Traffic is soft, or your customer count is flat.
body_md:
**Bring**
A list of customers not seen in the last 12 months, with their last visit and any deferred work.

**Word tracks**
- “Last time you were in, Hector graded your rear brakes in the yellow. Based on time and mileage, they're likely ready now. I'd like to get you in this week to take a look.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The rule: every call has a real reason
- 2:00 – Find the reason: deferred work, time and mileage, recall
- 4:00 – The word track
- 7:00 – Pairs: the 'I go somewhere else now' customer
- 11:00 – Ten calls each this week; post the count Friday

**Your move**
Pull the list tomorrow, and post the appointment count Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Prospecting/Under 5 mins/Prospect on the Way Out — The Household Vehicle
title: Prospect on the Way Out — The Household Vehicle
workbook_title: Prospect on the Way Out — The Household Vehicle
best_used_for: Your car count is flat, and your advisors treat every RO like it's the only vehicle in the family.
body_md:
**Bring**
A simple tally sheet for each workstation (household questions asked / vehicles added).

**Word tracks**
- “On the walk out, we prospect for every other vehicle in the household. We're not asking for a sale. We're planting a seed — we're the one place for the whole family.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Teach: prospect the household on the walk out
- 1:00 – Model the college-kid and spouse-vehicle lines
- 2:00 – Pair drill: catch the detail at write-up, use it at delivery
- 4:00 – Standard: ONE household question per delivery, tally inspected Friday

**Your move**
Put a tally on every workstation — household questions asked, vehicles added. Inspect it Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Prospecting/Under 5 mins/Recalls Are Visits
title: Recalls Are Visits
situation_tags: Slow traffic or prospecting|Phones and BDC
best_used_for: Your appointment board has holes, and you have open recalls on vehicles in your market.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your open recall list for vehicles in your market, split into ONE slice per advisor.

**Word tracks**
- “I'm calling because your manufacturer has an open recall on your vehicle. The repair is covered. I'd like to get you in this week, and while you're here, Hector will do a full inspection so you know exactly where everything stands.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The why: a recall is a full visit
- 1:00 – The call word track (manufacturer's voice)
- 2:00 – Book recalls into open slots, not the busiest morning
- 3:00 – Full walk-around and MPI on every recall visit
- 4:00 – Every slice worked this week; count appointments Friday

**Your move**
Hand out the slices tomorrow, and count the appointments set by Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Standards and Process/15 plus mins/Capacity — Shape the Day, Leave Room for Yes
title: Capacity — Shape the Day, Leave Room for Yes
workbook_title: Capacity — Shape the Day, Leave Room for Yes
situation_tags: Standards and process|Manager self-work|CSI and surveys
best_used_for: Your drive is full by nine, your next available appointment is a week out, and promise times are slipping.
body_md:
**Bring**
Two weeks of appointments by arrival time, hours sold vs. hours produced, and your next available appointment.

**Word tracks**
- “We're not booking fewer customers. We're booking them so every one gets the full visit.”

**Run sheet**
- Solo (20 min): arrival times; sold vs. produced; next available appointment
- Plan: stagger arrivals; mix the work; hold room for same-day yeses
- Team (10 min): share the new shape and why
- Daily: check next available and sold vs. produced before the huddle

**Your move**
Pull two weeks of arrival times and find your seven o'clock pile-up. *Academy: SMA 420 Capacity and Scheduling (weeks 43–45); revisited in SMA 401*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Standards and Process/5-15 mins/Digitize and Eliminate — Paper Is the Enemy of a Clean Drive
title: Digitize and Eliminate — Paper Is the Enemy of a Clean Drive
workbook_title: Digitize and Eliminate — Paper Is the Enemy of a Clean Drive
best_used_for: When paper is piling up — or a deferred item just got lost.
body_md:
**Set**
Workstation Standards

**Bring**
A handful of sticky notes or printouts collected from the drive (no customer info visible).

**Word tracks**
- “Every one of these is a customer's information. And every one of these can disappear under a coffee cup.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Hold up the paper: what's this costing us?
- 2:00 – Share the rule: if it matters, it goes in the system
- 4:00 – Where each item goes: DMS, notes field, phone, calendar
- 8:00 – Live: every advisor digitizes ONE item from their desk
- 11:00 – Standard and inspection

**Your move**
on your next desk walk, count the paper. Any desk with zero gets a shout-out at the next huddle.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Standards and Process/5-15 mins/Set the Standard Once — Then Hold It
title: Set the Standard Once — Then Hold It
workbook_title: Set the Standard Once — Then Hold It
best_used_for: When you launch — or relaunch — your workstation standard.
body_md:
**Set**
Workstation Standards

**Bring**
The written workstation standard, printed and ready to post, plus a photo of a desk that meets it.

**Word tracks**
- “This is our standard. I'm going to inspect it every week. Not to catch anybody — to make sure our customer sees our best every single time.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Why the standard matters to the customer
- 2:00 – Share the five-part standard
- 6:00 – Show it: the model desk
- 8:00 – Post it and set the inspection day
- 10:00 – Close: standards that aren't inspected are wishes

**Your move**
post the standard, then do your first inspection within seven days — and celebrate the first desk that nails it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Standards and Process/5-15 mins/Turn Class Guides Into Mini-Meetings
title: Turn Class Guides Into Mini-Meetings
best_used_for: Your team just sat through a forty-minute class. Great energy in the room. And two weeks later — nothing changed.
body_md:
**Bring**
The class guide, a highlighter, and five recent ROs per advisor for the Friday inspection.

**Word tracks**
- “This week we're doing ONE thing. Every customer gets a tire quote. Not most. Every.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the ONE concept from the guide and why it matters to the customer
- 2:00 – Manager models the word track
- 4:00 – Two advisors run it back out loud, word for word
- 7:00 – Set the standard and the Friday RO inspection
- 10:00 – Open the drive; repeat the same concept daily for 30 days

**Your move**
Open your last class guide. Circle ONE concept. Run it tomorrow morning before the doors open.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Standards and Process/5-15 mins/Waiters, Drop-Offs and Loaners — Use Them on Purpose
title: Waiters, Drop-Offs and Loaners — Use Them on Purpose
workbook_title: Waiters, Drop-Offs and Loaners — Use Them on Purpose
best_used_for: The lounge is full and frustrated, or waiters are eating your morning.
body_md:
**Bring**
Last week's waiter list with each job's actual time, and your loaner and shuttle use.

**Word tracks**
- “If you can leave it with us, we'll have Hector's full inspection done and text you the results by ten-thirty.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The waiter rule: only work you can finish while they wait
- 2:00 – Read last week's waiter list: promised vs. actual
- 5:00 – The drop-off invite word track
- 8:00 – Loaners and shuttle as capacity tools
- 10:00 – Lounge check
- 12:00 – Standard: a real time and an update before they ask

**Your move**
Track every waiter's promised time against the actual time for five days.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Standards and Process/5-15 mins/Walk the Drive Weekly
title: Walk the Drive Weekly
best_used_for: Same day every week. Before the drive opens.
body_md:
**Set**
Workstation Standards

**Bring**
A simple checklist: clear surface, nothing customer-readable, image behind the desk, no paper piling up.

**Word tracks**
- “Walked your desk this morning. Looks sharp — one thing: let's get those old ROs filed before the first customer.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Walk to the customer side of the first desk
- 2:00 – Inspect each workstation with fresh eyes
- 10:00 – Note fixes — no lectures
- 13:00 – Quick word with each advisor on ONE item

**Your move**
pick your day. Put it on your calendar as a recurring appointment. Walk every desk this week — from the customer's side.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Standards and Process/Under 5 mins/Don't Display Funky Filters in Front of an Audience
title: Don't Display Funky Filters in Front of an Audience
workbook_title: Don't Display Funky Filters in Front of an Audience
best_used_for: Your team is showing filters in the lounge, at the counter — in front of everybody.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE genuinely funky filter your shop pulled this week.

**Word tracks**
- “If you bring something with a bunch of dog food in it and show people that they've had a mouse or a squirrel in their vehicle, it could offend them in front of others.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Hold up the funky filter
- 1:00 – Mitch's line: why it can offend in front of others
- 2:00 – The rule: step away to see it privately
- 3:00 – Pass-the-filter drill, conditions not opinions
- 4:30 – Standard: private walk for funky filters

**Your move**
Watch the lounge. Catch ONE advisor making the private walk and call it out at Friday's huddle.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/5-15 mins/Name Tag Meeting
title: Name Tag Meeting
best_used_for: Mid-month. One-on-one, small group, or the whole squad.
body_md:
**Bring**
A dry erase board and markers, a name tag, and a list of the community activities your dealership sponsors.

**Word tracks**
- “You just told me that's why customers come here. So why aren't we promoting it on every visit?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Write 'WHY DO CUSTOMERS COME HERE?' on the board
- 1:00 – Dig for specifics; list every amenity and process
- 4:00 – Challenge: are we promoting these on every visit?
- 6:00 – The name tag: dealership name, manufacturer, title, name
- 11:00 – Feel-good close; pick ONE amenity to promote this week

**Your move**
Write the question on the board, pick the ONE amenity your team stopped promoting, and listen for it on every write-up.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/5-15 mins/Put Your Team on the 1000 Minute Rule
title: Put Your Team on the 1000 Minute Rule
workbook_title: Put Your Team on the 1000 Minute Rule
best_used_for: Monday. Start of the week. Especially when the drive feels busy but the numbers don't show it.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard.

**Word tracks**
- “You get about a thousand minutes today. Let's call every one of them a dollar. That's a thousand dollars. Where's it going?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the rule and the Serhant team angle
- 2:00 – Whiteboard math: 1,000 minutes, $1 a minute
- 4:00 – 'Where did your dollars go yesterday?' — manager goes first
- 8:00 – Make it vocabulary: 'How are we doing on our 1,000 today?'

**Your move**
Run it Monday. Then say "our 1,000" at least once a day, every day, until your advisors start saying it back to you.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/5-15 mins/Schedule Breaks Into the Drive — If It's Not on the Schedule It Doesn't Happen
title: Schedule Breaks Into the Drive — If It's Not on the Schedule It Doesn't Happen
workbook_title: Schedule Breaks Into the Drive — If It's Not on the Schedule It Doesn't Happen
best_used_for: Your advisors are sharp at 9 AM and going through the motions by 3 PM.
body_md:
**Bring**
A rotating break schedule you built before the meeting (10 AM / 12 PM / 3 PM with coverage partners).

**Word tracks**
- “A break is not laziness. It's maintenance. You'd never let a customer skip maintenance on their vehicle, and I'm not letting you skip it either.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Burkus step one: set a fixed time
- 2:00 – The 3 PM problem and why it's a CSI risk
- 4:00 – Share the rotating break schedule and coverage partners
- 6:00 – Walk through the other four steps
- 9:00 – Commit: breaks are protected even when the drive is slammed

**Your move**
Post the break schedule Monday. Protect it all week. Then watch your 3 PM deliveries.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/5-15 mins/The Brett Favre Problem — What Legacy Are You Leaving?
title: The Brett Favre Problem — What Legacy Are You Leaving?
workbook_title: The Brett Favre Problem — What Legacy Are You Leaving?
best_used_for: You've got veteran advisors who are crushing it — and new advisors drowning right next to them.
body_md:
**Bring**
Paper and pens; a list of proposed veteran/new-advisor pairs.

**Word tracks**
- “If you're an experienced advisor, the most valuable thing you have is what you know. What you choose to share — or not share — determines the quality of the team you leave behind.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The Favre/Rodgers story
- 2:00 – Veterans write down ONE thing a newer advisor doesn't know
- 4:00 – Round-robin share
- 8:00 – Set veteran/new pairs and the ONE-skill transfer
- 10:00 – Two-week check-in on the calendar

**Your move**
Set the pairs today. Put the two-week check-in on the calendar before you leave the room.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/5-15 mins/The ONE Word Meeting
title: The ONE Word Meeting
situation_tags: Team culture|Morale and recognition|New hire or onboarding
best_used_for: A new team, a new hire, or any time you want to know who your advisors really are.
body_md:
**Bring**
Blank business cards. Your ONE word with two real examples. ONE card per advisor with the word you picked for them and two or three dated moments. Twelve spark words in your pocket.

**Word tracks**
- “Take thirty seconds. Write down the ONE word that best describes what makes you, you. Not just as an advisor. As a person.”

**Run sheet**
- Day before (30 min): your word plus two examples; one card per advisor plus two or three dated moments; twelve spark words in your pocket
- 0:00 – Cards out; thirty seconds to write the ONE word
- 1:00 – If stuck: ten seconds, then five sparks
- 2:00 – Each advisor shares their word and why
- 6:00 – You share yours and how it guides you
- 8:00 – The payload: your word for each advisor, with evidence; hand over the card

**Your move**
Write your card and theirs, and run it before Friday. *Academy: SMA 401 Fixed Ops Financials (weeks 37–39); revisited in SMA 201*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/5-15 mins/What Is Your Team Measuring? — The Cup Diagnostic
title: What Is Your Team Measuring? — The Cup Diagnostic
workbook_title: What Is Your Team Measuring? — The Cup Diagnostic
best_used_for: In a team meeting, or a one-on-one, any time you want a real read on your culture. Not the survey version. The honest version.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing but the question — and the patience to sit in the silence after you ask it.

**Word tracks**
- “When you look at a teammate's performance, what are you measuring? Whether they have what they need to succeed — tools, coaching, clarity? Or whether they're ahead of you?”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Ask the measuring question, word for word
- 1:00 – Silence; let the team answer honestly
- 5:00 – Name the two cups: "do they have enough" vs. "are they ahead of me"
- 8:00 – Model it: contrast the two opening questions
- 10:00 – Commit: every one-on-one this week opens with "What do you need?"

**Your move**
Run the question in your next team meeting. Then, in every one-on-one this week, your first words are "What do you need?"

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/Under 5 mins/Don't Piggyback Off Your Advisor's Success
title: Don't Piggyback Off Your Advisor's Success
workbook_title: Don't Piggyback Off Your Advisor's Success
best_used_for: Any time you recognize an advisor's win — team meeting, one-on-one, hallway.
body_md:
**Set**
Coaching Investment

**Bring**
Nothing — just the specific result and the advisor's name.

**Word tracks**
- “You did that. Not we. Not the training. Not the platform. You. Did. That.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the advisor and the specific result
- 0:20 – Point at them: 'You did that'
- 0:40 – Step aside and let the room react
- 1:00 – Move on with the meeting — no 'we' callbacks later

**Your move**
Catch ONE win. Point at the person. Then get out of the frame.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/Under 5 mins/Highlight Winners — Recognition Drives Repetition
title: Highlight Winners — Recognition Drives Repetition
best_used_for: Every team meeting. Every group chat. Every manager message. Especially when you want more of a specific CSI behavior.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE specific CSI behavior you saw this week: the advisor's name, what they did, and what happened.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the advisor
- 0:15 – Name the specific behavior and what happened (not the survey score)
- 0:45 – Let it land: pause, applause, move on
- 1:00 – Rotate: a different name next week

**Your move**
Catch ONE advisor doing CSI right. Write down exactly what they did. Share it at your next meeting.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/Under 5 mins/Journal Complaints With Solutions
title: Journal Complaints With Solutions
best_used_for: Your team is venting about the same breakdown for the third time this week — and nothing is changing.
body_md:
**Bring**
A whiteboard, plus a notebook or one-page template with three lines: what happened, what it cost us, what I'd do about it.

**Word tracks**
- “From today on, nobody vents without a plan. If something is hurting our CSI, write it down.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the rule: no vent without a plan
- 1:00 – Write the three lines on the board
- 2:00 – Model one real journal entry
- 3:30 – Set the standard: ONE entry each by next meeting
- 4:30 – Close: you'll act on ONE solution

**Your move**
Run it Monday. Collect the entries Friday. Pick ONE solution and put it to work by the following Monday — so your team sees that writing it down actually moves something.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Team Culture and Morale/Under 5 mins/The Daily Micro-Goal With Personal Reward
title: The Daily Micro-Goal With Personal Reward
workbook_title: The Daily Micro-Goal With Personal Reward
situation_tags: Morale and recognition|Attach rate or ticket flat
best_used_for: Your advisors are going through the motions. The month feels long. The goals feel far away.
body_md:
**Bring**
Nothing. Pick the day's target service before the huddle.

**Word tracks**
- “Today, three A/C performance treatments each. One in the morning. One midday. One before close.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Name the micro-goal: three of ONE service, spread across the day
- 1:00 – Each advisor names their personal reward
- 2:30 – Break; midday check-in on the drive ('Where are you on your three?')
- End of day – Celebrate who hit three

**Your move**
Pick your service tonight. Set the three tomorrow morning. Check in at noon. Celebrate at close.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Technicians and the Shop/15 plus mins/Video MPI Meeting — Certified Technicians
title: Video MPI Meeting — Certified Technicians
best_used_for: Your certified technicians aren't sending video, or you're launching the video MPI.
body_md:
**Bring**
Wi-Fi tested in advance with a video created and sent yourself; a brand-new filter (or filter section) for each technician; a printed battery test result; a vehicle in a bay if you want to demo the shot list.

**Word tracks**
- “I want to know why doing a video multi-point inspection is a waste of time. Give me every reason.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Frame: we ARE doing the MPI; video the highlights. Wi-Fi demo
- 3:00 – 'Why is this a waste of time?' Collect every objection
- 6:00 – Answer: Wi-Fi, advisor's job, on camera, already inspecting
- 10:00 – Staging: the realtor analogy
- 12:00 – Shot list: front plate, battery printout, filter side-by-side, wipers, ONE tire/ONE pad, underneath, time/mileage last, end on name
- 18:00 – Standard: QC two videos per certified technician; announce video contest

**Your move**
Quality-check two videos per certified technician. A bad video loses business as fast as a good one earns it. Then run a contest on great videos. *Academy: SMA 420 Capacity and Scheduling (weeks 43–45); revisited in SMA 110*

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Technicians and the Shop/5-15 mins/Comebacks — Find the Cause, Not the Culprit
title: Comebacks — Find the Cause, Not the Culprit
workbook_title: Comebacks — Find the Cause, Not the Culprit
meeting_format: Advisor and technician, separately, then together
situation_tags: Technicians and the shop|Upset customers|CSI and surveys
best_used_for: The day any comeback hits the drive.
body_md:
**Bring**
The comeback RO, the original write-up, Hector's notes and any photo or video.

**Word tracks**
- “I'm sorry this came back. Hector is going to look at it first thing, and I'll text you by ten- thirty with what he finds.”

**Run sheet**
- Customer first: apology, Hector looks first thing, a text by a set time
- Hector, privately: 'What would have helped you catch it?'
- Advisor, privately: review the write-up; were the customer's words there?
- Together: ONE cause, ONE fix, written down
- Team: the lesson, never the name

**Your move**
On the next comeback, run all three conversations the same day.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Technicians and the Shop/5-15 mins/Coolant Top-Off Protocol
title: Coolant Top-Off Protocol
situation_tags: Technicians and the shop|Standards and process
best_used_for: Once, to set the policy. Then any time you see a hose near a radiator.
body_md:
**Bring**
A jug of distilled water and a printed 'Distilled Water Only' sign for each bay.

**Word tracks**
- “Starting today, distilled water only for every coolant top-off. No hose. No exceptions. There's a jug in every bay, and I'll keep them full.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Gather certified technicians and shop foreman in the bay
- 2:00 – Share the why: tap water minerals vs. the factory fill
- 5:00 – Announce the policy: distilled water only, every top-off
- 7:00 – Post signs and place a jug in every bay
- Friday – Spot check every bay

**Your move**
Set the policy Monday. Spot check every bay Friday. If there's no jug, that's on you — fill it.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Technicians and the Shop/5-15 mins/Show Technicians the Express Lane Math
title: Show Technicians the Express Lane Math
workbook_title: Show Technicians the Express Lane Math
situation_tags: Technicians and the shop|Attach rate or ticket flat
best_used_for: Technicians are resisting add-on services in your time-constrained lane.
body_md:
**Bring**
Your flag rate, a whiteboard, and a stopwatch.

**Word tracks**
- “That hour at your flag rate is real money in your paycheck. For less than three minutes of work. Do the math with your own flag rate.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Separate time from willingness; today is about time
- 1:00 – Put the math on the board: two services, ~2:15 of work, one hour of labor
- 3:00 – Techs do the paycheck math with their own flag rate
- 5:00 – Stopwatch demo on a vehicle in the lane
- 8:00 – Set the standard (offer both on every eligible vehicle) and Friday RO inspection

**Inspect it**
Inspect it Friday. Pull the ROs. Count the hours.

**Your move**
Run the stopwatch demo at your next tech meeting. Then post the hours by technician every day.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Technicians and the Shop/Under 5 mins/Ask Before You Promise — The Promise Time Belongs to Both Sides
title: Ask Before You Promise — The Promise Time Belongs to Both Sides
workbook_title: Ask Before You Promise — The Promise Time Belongs to Both Sides
situation_tags: Technicians and the shop|Standards and process|CSI and surveys
best_used_for: Promise times are slipping, or the shop is getting blamed for promises it never made.
body_md:
**Bring**
Last week's missed promise times, with the reason for each.

**Word tracks**
- “Anything bigger than routine maintenance, we check with the foreman before we give the customer a time. Ten seconds at the kiosk beats an angry call at four.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Read last week's missed promise times; no names, just reasons
- 1:00 – Standard: check with the foreman before promising anything bigger than routine
- 2:00 – Make the check easy: board or 11:00 stand-up
- 3:00 – Text the customer before you miss
- 4:00 – The foreman names ONE thing to fix

**Your move**
Start the eleven o'clock check tomorrow, and count missed promise times by Friday.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Technicians and the Shop/Under 5 mins/Close the Loop With Hector
title: Close the Loop With Hector
situation_tags: Technicians and the shop|Standards and process
best_used_for: Your certified technicians stop sending video. Or they ask, "Does anybody even look at these?"
body_md:
**Bring**
Yesterday's graded reds and whether each technician heard the customer's decision.

**Word tracks**
- “Every red Hector grades, he hears the customer's decision within the hour. Approved or deferred. Every one.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The count: reds graded vs. decisions shared
- 1:00 – The standard: every decision back to the technician within the hour
- 2:00 – The why: no feedback, thinner inspections
- 3:00 – Pick ONE way to close the loop
- 4:00 – Ask the technicians what would help most

**Your move**
Track every red for five days. Friday, ask Hector if anything changed.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Technicians and the Shop/Under 5 mins/Know Every Technician's Specialty — By Name
title: Know Every Technician's Specialty — By Name
workbook_title: Know Every Technician's Specialty — By Name
situation_tags: Technicians and the shop|Objections and deferred work
best_used_for: Your team is losing recommendations to pushback, and every answer sounds the same.
body_md:
**Bring**
A roster of every certified technician with ONE impressive, true fact about each, built with your shop foreman ahead of time.

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – Quick test: name the techs, then their specialties
- 1:00 – Model generic vs. by-name-plus-specialty
- 2:00 – Hand out the roster, name by name
- 3:00 – Rapid-fire pushback drill
- 4:30 – Standard: ONE fact per technician; Friday pop quiz

**Your move**
Friday, walk up to ONE advisor and name a technician. They've got five seconds to share that technician's specialty.

classification_line: Manager Meetings/Technicians and the Shop/Under 5 mins/The Drive-and-Shop Huddle
title: The Drive-and-Shop Huddle
best_used_for: Once a week, same day, same time. Advisors and certified technicians, together.
body_md:
**Bring**
ONE photo or video MPI from last week that led to a yes, and ONE question from the shop.

**Word tracks**
- “Hector graded it. Maria shared it. The customer said yes. That's how it's supposed to work.”

**Run sheet**
- 0:00 – The win: play ONE photo or video that led to a yes; name the technician and the advisor
- 1:30 – The shop's ONE question
- 2:30 – ONE fix, with a name and a day
- 3:30 – The drive's ONE ask
- 4:30 – Back to work

**Your move**
Pick the day and the time, and hold the first one in the shop.
